Started 2026-11-15. The owner asked me to plan and then "manage threads (GPT-6-LUNA high)" to implement a phone layout modelled on a reference mail app's screenshots, validate with screenshots, and "continue until you have a working version for me to test out". Follows on from [[maintenance-programme]] (closed).

**Threads:** `t3_thread_launch`, provider/instance `codex`, model `gpt-6-luna`, option `reasoningEffort: high`, runtime full-access, worktree from `origin/mobile/integration`.

**Owner decisions (2026-11-15):**
- No Tailwind migration (my recommendation, accepted). Compact CSS goes in `src/assets/mobile/*.css` scoped under `.app[data-layout="compact"]`.
- UI only over existing features. Out of scope: calendar, AI/voice, send, HTML bodies, label chips, multiple splits, trash/spam/move, reply-all, forward. Inbox zero = plain empty state, no photo.

**Merge authority (my interpretation, not stated by the owner):** phase PRs target the branch `mobile/integration`; I review, gate and merge them into that branch. I do NOT merge to `main`; a PR `mobile/integration` → `main` is for the owner (and gives CI + the APK artifact, since CI only runs on PRs based on main).

**Reference screenshots:** `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-refs/01..10-*.jpg`. They contain the owner's private mail: never commit or upload them.

**Phases:** P1 foundations + shell frame (layout mode `useLayoutMode`, tokens, top bar/bottom bar, system bars, Back, rendered harness at 412×915) → then two parallel tracks: list (rows, split pill, drawer, swipes, long-press selection) and reader (bottom action bar, overflow sheet, message menu, undo toast, full-screen compose + keyboard) → remaining surfaces (search, reminders, drafts, account, activity, provider mail) + settings → my integrated emulator validation and APK for the owner.

**Validation setup:** emulator device host `local`, id `emulator-5554` (t3-pixel, Android 15, 1080×2400), package `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`; use T3 device tools. Chrome for rendered tests: `/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome`. Machine: 4 cores, 15 GB, ~10 GB free disk; shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, one heavy command at a time, at most two threads.

**State 2026-11-15 15:25 UTC:** `mobile/integration` pushed at f605bc1 (= main). P1 thread running: `mcp:launch:d2dfe6e91811e8a341ba49fc84e906bc3c3c0ea764a10fefbf3b39acd487c70d`, branch `mobile/p1-foundations`.

**How GPT-6 Luna (high) behaves here (learned 2026-11-15, 15:25–16:15 UTC):** turns are short (seconds to ~4 min); it stops and reports "not complete" on a large step, stops right after `view_image`, tries the repo's `implement` skill (which wants a feature-engineer agent) and gives up at the first obstacle. Queued big steps burn as no-op turns. What works: a checklist file outside the repo (`/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p2-<track>/PROGRESS.md`, ~16–19 small items, each with its own check, "tick, commit, push") plus identical queued nudges ("Continue with PROGRESS.md: first unticked item…"), about one item per turn. Always tell it: no `implement` skill, no delegation, no `view_image`, no cargo/Android builds, code style (it writes minified one-liners unless told), retry pushes (remote pack errors are transient). I do the visual review (screenshots via `mise run screenshots:mobile`, test `tests/layout/mobile-screenshots.rendered.test.ts`, which I wrote) and all Android builds.

**Android build from a worktree:** the shared cargo target does not regenerate Tauri's Kotlin sources in a new worktree; copy `src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/*` from the root checkout first (`cp -n`). My build checkout: `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-validate` (worktree, detached). Build ~35–90 s: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run android:build`. The emulator's app was a CI-signed APK; I backed up its data to `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/emulator-appdata-before-local-apk-2026-11-15.tar`, uninstalled it and installed the locally signed build. One hang at "Checking the demo mailbox…" on the first launch right after install (not reproduced after `pm clear`); retest before handing over.

**State 2026-11-15 16:15 UTC:** P1 merged into `mobile/integration` (PR #75 + my fix commit + context-host prep; head 58ca5a9): layout mode, tokens, top bar, bottom bar with `backHost`/`actionsHost`/`contextHost`, dark system bars, Back via `window.__emailOsAndroidBack`, rendered tests 53/53, unit 1,909. Verified on the emulator: bars, compact frame, Back closes reader then backgrounds. Running: list track `mcp:launch:e4c090dc6cc0fc8fafd367a73aee4d879ff1b6b411e9c31b163528aa6b7a5491` (branch `mobile/p2-list`) and reader track `mcp:launch:817c514889e48621ca24bb86808f079e535512c3aaed7c31b2ee5b1be2475a7c` (branch `mobile/p2-reader`), both on checklists. After them: remaining surfaces (search, reminders, drafts, account/activity/provider mail pages, settings with swipe prefs), then integrated APK for the owner.

**State 2026-11-15 20:45 UTC:** `mobile/integration` = a574927: P1 + list track (PR #77: stacked rows, split pill, navigation drawer `MobileDrawer.vue`, swipes `useSwipeAction.ts`, long-press selection) + reader track (PR #76: compact reader toolbar with star/more, `MobileActionSheet.vue`, reply bar, per-message menu, toast, compose sheet), merged by me with conflicts resolved (App.vue, main.ts, css-contract, HeaderGlyph, mise.toml, DESIGN.md). Merged tree: unit 1,947 in 116 files, rendered 67/67, build OK. Emulator check of a574927 (local APK): rows, swipe-left done + Undo, swipe-right reminder picker, reader, Back all work with real touch; real keyboard (Gboard) resizes the WebView correctly. Running: fix round in the old reader thread `mcp:launch:817c5148…` on branch `mobile/p2-fixes` (checklist `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p2-fixes/PROGRESS.md`, 12 items: reply/compose sheets must cover the app, focused-row date, selection checkboxes and bar, nav pill background, keyboard-height case) and pages track `mcp:launch:8aabfbb166f97f301710f04e10311dff2916e8927a63357130ed5c98b354c9f3` on `mobile/p3-pages` (checklist `…/p3-pages/PROGRESS.md`, 15 items: drafts, reminders, picker sheet, search, utility pages, palette, contact, swipe preferences, settings). After both: merge into integration, full gates, APK, emulator pass, open PR `mobile/integration` → `main` for the owner, hand over the APK path.
- Emulator IME: I switched the default input method from the device tool's hidden helper (`com.callstack.agentdevice.imehelper/.TestInputMethodService`) to Gboard with `adb shell ime set` to see the real keyboard. Restore the helper when validation is finished.
- `agent-device` tips: `gesture pan <x> <y> <dx> <dy> <ms>` in device pixels does a real swipe; `press <x> <y>` taps; a programmatic focus does not raise the keyboard, a tap does.

**State 2026-11-16 01:35 UTC: FIRST WORKING VERSION DELIVERED.** `mobile/integration` = 645d731 (P1 #75, list #77, reader #76, fixes #78, pages #79, polish #81, plus my merges, a typecheck fix and a docs commit with emulator screenshots in `docs/validation/mobile/`). PR #80 `mobile/integration` → `main` is open and ready for review; the owner merges it (I do not). Unit 1,959 in 118 files, rendered 76/76, build OK, CI `check` + `android-apk` green on b7b2637 (645d731 is docs-only on top). Emulator has the locally built APK of b7b2637 installed (fresh install, fixture data, one draft); IME restored to the device tool's helper; airplane mode, which a stray tap of mine had turned on, is off again. No threads running.
- Open items reported to the owner, not fixed: first launch right after a fresh install can ANR (pre-existing since #63; relaunch is fine); Contact page header still says "Close" as text; "Contact details" row uses the menu glyph; no physical-device test; I reviewed by tests, screenshots and device, and spot-read the code, not every line.
- Lesson: before coordinate taps or `back` on the emulator, confirm the app is in the foreground (snapshot shows the webview title). `back` at the app root backgrounds it and the next taps land on whatever is behind (they landed in Android Settings).
**Round 2, started 2026-11-16 ~21:30 UTC (critique fixes).** The owner asked for an Impeccable critique of the key phone screens run by Sonnet 5.5 subagents; result 25/40 (snapshot in `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-validate/.impeccable/critique/2026-11-16T07-24-15Z__src-assets-mobile.md`, not committed). Owner's answers: fix selection and swipes first; scope = all five priority issues, not the minor ones; editor = "Remove the Save and Close button and only use the X button and a fixed sentence" (my reading: X is the only exit on the phone, "never sent" is the fixed phrase, save-state words stay truthful); builders = GPT-6 Luna threads again. CI on 645d731 is green.
- Three tracks reuse the old Luna threads and worktrees on new branches from `origin/mobile/integration`, with checklists in `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p5-{list,editor,pages}/PROGRESS.md`: list thread (`mcp:launch:e4c090dc…`) → `mobile/p5-list` (selected-row fill, two-row selection bar, swipe tracking/armed state/row exit, reduced motion); reader thread (`mcp:launch:817c5148…`) → `mobile/p5-editor` ("never sent", phone keyboard attributes, X-only exit, failure state, new glyphs copy/collapse/contact/prompt, accent on done); pages thread (`mcp:launch:8aabfbb1…`) → `mobile/p5-pages` (Back header on pushed pages, Settings hierarchy and immediate save, search insets, syntax disclosure), started only after one of the first two finishes (two-thread limit).
- After the tracks: I review screenshots (`p5-*/` dirs), merge PRs into `mobile/integration`, run gates, rebuild the APK, check on the emulator, update PR #80, re-run the critique for the score. Progress helper: `scratchpad/p5.sh` of session 415cd333.
- Review directories: `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/` (`final/` browser screenshots, `final-android/` emulator screenshots, per-track `PROGRESS.md` checklists).
- **State 2026-11-17 19:25 UTC:** all three round-2 tracks merged into `mobile/integration` = 0388d56 (PR #82 editor, #83 list, #84 pages). Gates on 0388d56: unit 1,990/121 files, rendered 81 (+5 skipped), build OK. Local APK of 0388d56 on the emulator. Emulator found two device-only issues, sent as follow-ups: list thread → `mobile/p5-list-2` (checklist `p5-list2/PROGRESS.md`: hide split pill while selecting, notice above the selection bar); pages thread → `mobile/p5-pages-2` (`p5-pages/PROGRESS-2.md`: pushed pages used `inset: 24px` = the browser preview's account-tab strip height, so on Android they sat 24px low with the top bar peeking through). Lesson: browser screenshots include a ~24px fixture account strip that the APK lacks; check page offsets on the device.
- The first launch after `install` showed the known ANR again ("Wait" then relaunch works). Two fixture rows were marked done by my swipe tests (Lunch Thursday?, Perf notes).
- **State 2026-11-17 20:05 UTC: ROUND 2 DELIVERED.** `mobile/integration` = f08fd85 (adds #85 selection replaces split pill, #86 pushed pages `position:absolute; inset:0` with `.app-main` static in compact + Android Back closes search form and reminder picker + Back audit test `tests/layout/mobile-android-back.test.ts`). Unit 2,004/122, rendered 82 + 6 skipped (one unidentified flaky failure in 1 of 5 runs), build OK, CI green on f08fd85. PR #80 description updated with a "Round 2" section. Emulator has the local APK of f08fd85. No threads running. Not done: re-running the critique for a new score (offered to the owner); expired-Undo notice lingering on screen (pre-existing, reported).
- **Critique round 3, 2026-11-17 20:35 UTC:** owner asked for a critique by 3 GPT-6.1-SOL sub-agents (codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoningEffort high, via `delegate_task`). Result 25/40, P1 ×4 (lingering "Undo expired" notice; unlabelled reader dock; hidden selection entry + "loaded" scope + 40px primary; Contact 24px targets) + P2 swipe (fling commit before armed cue, glyph by direction not configured action). Raw reviews in `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/critique-r2/`. Owner answers: fix the lingering Undo-expired notice first; scope = all four P1s + swipe P2; reader bar = label Done only (keep six controls). The reviewer's "Save and close text instead of X" was excluded (conflicts with the owner's X-only decision). Next: implementation not yet started; offer it (Luna threads were the builders last time).
- **Round P6 started 2026-11-17 ~20:50 UTC.** Owner: "split the steps across threads (GPT-6.2-SOL) until the changes are done and then run impeccable critique with 3 subagents (GPT-6.2-Astra, GPT-6.2-SOL, Opus 5.5)". Threads: codex `gpt-6.2-sol`, reasoningEffort high (my choice), worktrees from origin/mobile/integration. Rules `/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/P6-RULES.md`; checklists `p6-notice-swipe/` (thread A `mcp:launch:66a3d3c4…`), `p6-reader-contact/` (thread B `mcp:launch:8f301e6e…`), `p6-selection/` (track C, start after A merges: shares list.css/InboxList/App). Threads are told to run all items in one turn. Then: review screenshots, merge PRs, gates, APK + emulator, update PR #80, critique with Astra + SOL (delegate_task, codex) + Opus 5.5 (native Agent).
- **P6 delivered + critique r3, 2026-11-17 21:45 UTC.** `mobile/integration` = ac939a3 (#87 notices end quietly + swipe cue/icon, #88 labelled Done + Contact, #89 Select button/empty mode/"N of M selected"). Unit 2,042, rendered 86+6 skipped, CI green on ac939a3, PR #80 body has a "Round 3" section. Emulator has the APK of ac939a3. GPT-6.2-SOL threads: fast (all items in one turn) but twice stopped on codex approval requests (writing temp files in /tmp / gh) that I cannot approve; fix = restart the turn telling it not to escalate and to keep temp files inside the worktree. Critique r3 (A1 gpt-6.2-sol, A2 Opus 5.5 native Agent, B gpt-6.2-astra) = 25/40 again; top P1s: disabled reader glyphs look live (my round-2 `opacity:1; color:--icon-muted`), swipes active in selection mode, swipe-setting failure leaves radio checked, silent endings (Undo deadline/handoff, editor X "draft kept"). Raw in `critique-r3/`. Awaiting owner's choice of next scope.
- agent-device lesson: element refs (@eN) go stale after `screenshot`; re-snapshot before pressing a ref, or press by coordinates.
- Owner answers to critique r3 (2026-11-18): fix the search form over the Inbox first; endings stay SILENT (no Undo countdown, no "Moved to Done", no "Draft kept"); scope = the 4 P1s + search P2, which with silent endings means: search form, disabled-vs-live reader controls (+48px reader Back), no swipes in selection mode (+ one arm/commit distance rule), swipe-setting failure restores the radio. Not started yet.
- **P7 started 2026-11-18** ("Go ahead"): track D search (`p7-search/PROGRESS.md`, branch mobile/p7-search, thread `mcp:launch:8f301e6e…`), track E controls (`p7-controls/PROGRESS.md`, branch mobile/p7-controls, thread `mcp:launch:66a3d3c4…`), both gpt-6.2-sol high, parallel. P6-RULES.md now forbids escalation and /tmp temp files. After: merge, gates, APK, emulator, PR #80 update; the owner did not ask for another critique this time.
- **P7 delivered 2026-11-18 ~06:35 UTC.** `mobile/integration` = d76aab2 (#90 controls: live/disabled reader glyphs, 48px reader Back, no swipes while selecting, single swipe distance max(128px, 35%), swipe-setting failure restores radio (compact only); #91 search form alone, "Search mail" placeholder, example in syntax help). Unit 2,045, rendered 88+6 skipped, APK built and checked on the emulator. CI on d76aab2: android-apk passed, `check` still running when I reported. PR #80 body has "Round 4". Desktop swipe-settings failure still leaves the radio checked (out of compact scope). No threads running.
- **Critique r4, 2026-11-18 07:40 UTC** (owner: "Spin up subagents to run impeccable critique"; I reused the r3 trio for comparability): 26/40 (A1 26, A2 27). P1s: small targets (Details summary ~20px, quote toggle, Cached mail only label); reminder sheet hidden Enter step + verbose presets (flagged in every run); dock height not in list end padding + notice double margin. P2s: Commands acts on unnamed row / swipe verb at 128px; browser-blue radios + Files and links always disabled outside Android (App.vue:907 uses actionAvailable('open')). Raw in `critique-r4/`. Awaiting owner's choice.
- Owner answers to critique r4 (2026-11-18): reminder sheet first; scope = 3 P1s + 2 P2s; keep reader "Unread" as is (Mark read stays in More). Not started yet.

content.text:
The phone interface is done, but the Android app can't open your real mail yet. It's built as a demo app and only ever shows the 18 sample conversations. Nothing has changed on `main` since PR #80 merged on 19 November.

## What stops you from reading your Gmail on the phone

1. **Android is locked to the demo mailbox.** `src-tauri/src/setup.rs:40-41` always picks the sample data on mobile. The switch to Gmail (`EMAIL_OS_MODE`) only exists on desktop. Even the app's ID says so: `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`.
2. **There's nowhere on Android to keep your login.** Login tokens are only saved to the macOS Keychain. On every other platform, Android included, the store just fails (`crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs:119`), and there's deliberately no plain-file fallback. Android needs storage backed by its own secure keystore.
3. **Google sign-in only works the desktop way.** It opens a temporary listener on the computer for Google to send you back to, and reads the app's Google ID from an environment variable at launch (`crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs`). On a phone the usual approach is to open Google in the browser and have it return to the app through a link, using a Google app ID set up for Android and built into the app.
4. **Product decision.** ADR 0001 says "No custom Android surface in this build". Gmail on Android goes beyond that, so the ADR should be updated on purpose.

## What will bother you even with Gmail connected

- **No sending, on any platform.** Writing a message or reply only saves a draft on the device, and drafts don't sync to Gmail. You could sort mail in Email OS and send from the Gmail app.
- **No HTML display.** The reader shows plain text only, and most real mail is HTML.
- **No saving attachments or opening links on Android.** Both are switched off there (`src-tauri/src/commands/attachments.rs`).

## Installing and reliability

- **Test builds only.** The app is signed with whichever key built it, and CI and my machine use different keys. You can't install a new version over one signed by the other key, so switching means uninstalling and losing the app's data. Easy updates need one permanent signing key.
- **The first launch after a fresh install can freeze** with Android's "isn't responding" message. Opening it again works. This dates from PR #63 and was seen again in later rounds.
- **Never run on a real phone or an ARM64 device.** It has only been tested on the x86_64 Android 15 emulator.

## Agreed polish that hasn't started

Round 5 from the fourth design review: you said the reminder sheet goes first, plus small tap targets, the bottom spacing around the action bar, the Commands menu acting on a row it doesn't name, and the browser-blue radio buttons. These are nice to have, not blockers.

**Suggested order:** first a permanent signing key, the first-launch freeze and a real-phone test, which are quick. Then Gmail on Android (secure login storage, phone-style sign-in, a mode switch and the ADR update), which is the real work. Then HTML display, and sending last.

If you only want to sort mail on the phone and reply from Gmail, steps 1–3 above are enough. Do you want that, or do you also need sending? I can plan the work from your answer.

# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Implemented (stages 1–4). Stage 4 landed with the owner's decisions below: the default switched to the synthetic core, the legacy `MailCore` backend, its store and worker and the `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE` opt-in were removed, and the one-time transition is the `fixture_transition` state machine behind the startup gate. The sections below are the original investigation and are kept as the record of why.

## Decisions

Taken on 2026-11-14 on the coordinating thread's recommendation, after the project owner asked for the remaining maintenance tickets to run. They authorise **stages 1 to 3** only. The owner can still redirect before stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the legacy backend); nothing below is a user-facing change until then.

1. **Staged unification**, as recommended above. The legacy `MailCore` backend stays the default and is not touched until stage 4.
2. **The unified fixture gains read and star.** Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the "archive-only" wording in the stages and inventory below, which was about preserving today's errors. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. **Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules** (hide locally, no provider write). The legacy fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. **The on-disk transition (stage 4) is a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup**, local drafts untouched. It is planned, not implemented, in stages 1–3.

### Stage 4 decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)

5. **Interrupted writes are requeued by the synthetic policy.** A write interrupted before the provider recorded it is reconciled against the provider's durable facts at startup: landed means confirmed, unlanded means requeued and applied again. This matches the legacy fixture and is a session-policy method (`replay_unlanded_interrupted_writes`), not a mode check. Gmail keeps its rule of never replaying on its own.
6. **Read, star, Starred, Retry and read state are shown by capability, not by mode name.** `AccountStatus.capabilities.triageSurfaces` states it explicitly (a synthetic session sets it; Gmail leaves the field absent and clients keep their previous behaviour). The seeded Inbox is a realistic read/unread mix: the user's own messages are read, conversations whose newest message the user wrote are read (`conv-02`, `conv-04`, `conv-14`, `conv-16`), a few others are read (`conv-03`, `conv-10`), the two initially archived conversations are read, and the remaining 10 of the 16 Inbox conversations are unread.
7. **The one-time reset is disclosed on a startup gate** backed by two new IPC commands (status and accept). Backup, reset and the failure paths are described in the stage 4 plan and implemented with the transition state machine.
8. **Reminders** keep the Gmail local rules; copy for the retired archive/restore phases and any fixture text that became untrue is updated. Provider-flavoured error copy does not appear for fixture operations.

Unchanged by these decisions: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present (including the two initially archived `conv-06` and `conv-15`), and the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

# Rules for the "usable Android app" tracks (read before you start)

Repository: Email OS (Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + TypeScript, Rust core in `crates/mail-core`, shell in `src-tauri`).
GitHub: `BbrSofiane/email-os`. A coordinator thread reviews your work; it talks to you through messages in your thread.

There are four tracks, each in its own worktree and branch from `origin/main`:

| Track | ADR number | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| A. Install and run (signing key, package, first-launch ANR, real devices) | 0003 | `usable/install` |
| B. Google sign-in on Android | 0004 | `usable/android-gmail` |
| C. HTML mail display | 0005 | `usable/html-reader` |
| D. Sending (macOS desktop and Android) | 0006 | `usable/send` |

Use only your own ADR number so the four files do not collide. Read the other tracks' rows so you know who owns what; if your design needs something from another track, write it under "Dependencies" in your ADR instead of building it yourself.

## Phase 1: ADR proposal (now)

1. Read `docs/current-status.md`, `docs/current-architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/adr/0001-*.md`, `docs/adr/0002-*.md` and the code your area touches.
2. Write `docs/adr/000N-<short-slug>.md` (the number from the table). Match the tone of ADR 0002: plain, factual, no marketing. Status: `Proposed`. Sections:
   - **Context**: what exists today, with file:line references.
   - **Options considered**: at least two real options, with trade-offs.
   - **Decision** (proposed): the option you recommend, and why.
   - **Scope / out of scope.**
   - **Owner actions**: anything only the owner can do (Google Cloud console, GitHub secrets, a keystore password, a physical phone). Say exactly what and when it is needed. Never invent credentials, client IDs or keys.
   - **Dependencies** on other tracks, and what they need from you.
   - **Implementation plan**: ordered stages, each small enough for one sub-agent run, each with its own check (test, command or screenshot).
   - **Validation plan**: unit/integration tests, browser screenshots, Android emulator screenshots and screen recordings (videos) where the change is visible or a flow.
   - **Risks and open questions** for the owner.
3. Commit, push the branch (retry on transient remote errors), and end your turn with one line: `ADR READY: docs/adr/000N-....md @ <commit sha>`, followed by a short summary and your open questions.
4. Do **not** start implementing. No cargo or Android builds in this phase. Wait for a message from the coordinator: either review comments (revise, push, report `ADR READY` again) or `GREENLIGHT`.

## Phase 2: implementation (only after GREENLIGHT)

- Split the implementation plan into stages and hand each stage to a sub-agent with `delegate_task`: provider instance `codex`, model `gpt-6.1-terra`, option `reasoningEffort: high`, working in **your** worktree (no new checkout). Run stages one after another, not in parallel, in the same worktree. Give each sub-agent: these rules, the ADR, the exact stage, its check, and "commit when the check passes; do not push; no further delegation".
- After each stage, **review it yourself**: read the diff, run the stage's check, and fix or send it back. You own the result.
- When all stages pass: run the full gates (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`, plus the rendered tests below), do the validation plan (screenshots and videos), set the ADR status to `Accepted` with the decisions taken, update `docs/current-status.md` and `docs/development.md` where they change, push, and open a PR to `main`: `gh pr create -R BbrSofiane/email-os --base main`. The PR body lists what changed, the gates run with results, and the validation evidence (paths to screenshots/videos).
- End your turn with: `READY FOR REVIEW: <PR url> @ <head sha>` and the open items. The coordinator reviews and merges; you do not merge.

## Machine limits (shared by all tracks)

- 4 cores, 15 GB RAM, ~8 GB free disk. Only two tracks implement at the same time; the coordinator decides which.
- Rust: always `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`. One heavy command (cargo build/test, Android build, full test suite) at a time: before one, check `pgrep -fa 'cargo|gradle|vitest'`; if another track is building, wait and retry.
- Android build from a worktree: first `cp -n /home/exedev/email-os/src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/* src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/` (the shared target does not regenerate these), then `mise run android:build`.
- Do not create large files outside your worktree. Delete build outputs you no longer need.

## Android emulator (shared, one track at a time)

- Device host `local`, id `emulator-5554` (Android 15, x86_64, 1080×2400). Drive it with the T3 device tools (`device_open`, then the returned `agent-device` command; `device_screenshot`). `adb` only for install, logs and `run-as` file checks.
- Lock: before using it, create `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/emulator.lock` containing your branch name (`set -o noclobber; echo usable/xyz > …/emulator.lock`). If it exists and is not yours, wait. Remove it when done. Leave the app installed and the emulator as you found it (input method, airplane mode off).
- Before coordinate taps or `back`, confirm the app is in the foreground. Element refs (`@eN`) go stale after a screenshot: re-snapshot first.
- Screen recordings: `agent-device record` (see `help record`). Keep videos short (≤60 s).

## Validation evidence

- Browser screenshots: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR=<dir> mise run screenshots:mobile`. Rendered tests: `EMAIL_OS_RUN_RENDERED=1 EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=<same chrome> pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts <file>`.
- Put committed evidence under `docs/validation/<track-slug>/` (small PNGs; videos only if under ~5 MB, otherwise keep them in `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/<track-slug>/` and list the path in the PR).
- Synthetic data only in anything committed. Never commit real mail, tokens, client secrets, keystores or passwords. Never open any directory named `email-os-mobile-refs`.

## Working style

- Readable multi-line code that matches the surrounding style; no minified one-liners. Tests next to the existing ones.
- Product voice: terse and factual; never claim more than the app knows (pending, confirmed, failed and unknown stay distinct). No third-party brand names in UI copy.
- Do not use the repo's `implement` skill. Delegate only as described in phase 2.
- You run with full access. Never request escalated or sandbox-bypass permissions (nobody can approve them and you will stall). Keep temporary files inside your worktree (e.g. under `.git/`), not in `/tmp`. Pass PR bodies inline or from a file inside the worktree.
- If you are blocked on something only the owner can provide, say `BLOCKED:` with the exact need and stop; do not work around it with fake values.

You own track A of the "usable Android app" programme: everything about installing and running the Android app day to day. First read /home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md in full and follow it. You are in phase 1: write ADR 0003 as a proposal, push it, report `ADR READY`, and stop. Do not implement until I send GREENLIGHT.

Today the Android app is a debug APK signed with whichever key built it (CI and local builds differ), so an update from the other source fails with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE and the only way forward is uninstall, which loses the app's data. The package ID is `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`. The goal: the owner installs the app on their own phone and can update it without losing data.

The ADR must cover at least:
- A stable signing key: release vs debug build, where the keystore lives, how CI signs (GitHub Actions secrets, which the owner adds), how local builds sign, key backup, and what happens to existing installs.
- Package ID and app name: keep `androidfixture` or move to a final ID now (once track B adds real Gmail, "fixture" is wrong). Moving later costs another reinstall; Google's Android OAuth client is bound to package name + signing-certificate SHA-1, which track B needs from you. Recommend one.
- Versioning (versionCode/versionName from the repo), and how the owner gets new builds (CI artifact download, GitHub Releases, or other), including whether updates keep data.
- ABI coverage: the phone is most likely ARM64; the build makes ARM64 and x86_64. Release APK size, minify/shrink.
- The first-launch ANR after a fresh install ("Input dispatching timed out ... Waited 5000ms for FocusEvent", see docs/current-status.md "Android unified-fixture smoke"). Investigate the startup path (src-tauri/src/setup.rs, profile open, fixture_transition, frontend boot) and propose a cause and fix, or a way to find it, without running builds in this phase.
- Anything else that blocks installing and running on a real phone (permissions, backup rules/`allowBackup`, network security config needed later by tracks B and D, app icon/label, splash).
- A validation plan on the emulator and on the owner's physical phone (as an owner action with exact steps).

Report back with `ADR READY: ...` and your open questions.

input.title: Usable B: Google sign-in on Android (ADR 0004)
input.message:
You own track B of the "usable Android app" programme: Google sign-in and real Gmail on Android. First read /home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md in full and follow it. You are in phase 1: write a NEW ADR 0004 as a proposal (the owner wants a new ADR, not an edit of ADR 0001; it may say which parts of 0001 it supersedes, e.g. "No custom Android surface in this build"), push it, report `ADR READY`, and stop. Do not implement until I send GREENLIGHT.

Today:
- Android is hard-wired to the synthetic fixture (src-tauri/src/setup.rs, `#[cfg(mobile)] let mode = "fixture"`). Desktop picks Gmail only through `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`.
- Tokens are stored only in the macOS Keychain (crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs; every other platform returns SecretsUnavailable, no plaintext fallback by design).
- OAuth is the desktop loopback flow with PKCE, a 127.0.0.1 listener and the client id from the launch environment (crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs, GoogleConfig::from_env). Read-only scope first, `gmail.modify` as an explicit upgrade.
- Attachment export and external link dispatch are off on Android (src-tauri/src/commands/attachments.rs).

The ADR must cover at least:
- The sign-in flow on Android: system browser / Custom Tabs + redirect back to the app (custom scheme vs verified App Link), or the platform credential APIs; which Google OAuth client type (Android client bound to package + SHA-1 from track A, or another type) and how the client id gets into the build (no launch env on a phone). How the Rust core's PKCE/token code is reused.
- Secure token storage on Android (Android Keystore-backed), how it plugs into the `Secrets` trait, behaviour on reinstall/backup, and no plaintext fallback.
- Mode selection on Android: how the user goes from the demo mailbox to Gmail (and back / disconnect), first-run UX on the phone layout, and what the fixture becomes.
- Scopes: read-only first and the modify upgrade as today; track D (sending) will need `gmail.send` — define the scope-upgrade mechanism so D can request it, but D owns the send consent itself.
- Network/background behaviour on Android: sync while the app is open, app backgrounded/killed, connectivity loss, battery; what is out of scope (push notifications?).

- Google Cloud owner actions with exact steps (OAuth consent screen, test users vs verification for restricted Gmail scopes, Android client with package name and SHA-1).
- Validation: emulator screenshots and a screen recording of the sign-in flow; what can be tested without the owner's Google account and what needs it.

input.title: Usable C: HTML mail display (ADR 0005)
input.message:
You own track C of the "usable Android app" programme: displaying HTML mail. First read /home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md in full and follow it. You are in phase 1: write ADR 0005 as a proposal, push it, report `ADR READY`, and stop. Do not implement until I send GREENLIGHT.

Today the reader is plain-text only on every platform (docs/current-status.md: "HTML mail rendering are not implemented"); most real mail is HTML, some with no text part. The reader must work in both the desktop layout and the phone (compact) layout, in the Tauri webview on macOS and Android, and in the browser preview.

The ADR must cover at least:
- Where the HTML comes from: what the Gmail sync stores today (bodies, MIME parts, size bounds, cache) and what must change in crates/mail-core to keep the HTML part; text/plain vs text/html choice and fallback when there is no text part.
- Safety: sanitising (in Rust or in the frontend; which library), isolation (sandboxed iframe with srcdoc, CSP, no scripts, no forms, no same-origin), and no access to Tauri IPC from mail content.
- Remote content: images and other remote resources blocked by default (tracking pixels), a per-message "load images" choice and whether it is remembered; `cid:` inline images from attachments.
- Links: they must go through the app's existing explicit link confirmation (links are disabled on Android today; say what HTML links do there and coordinate with track B, which owns the Android gates).
- Layout: fitting wide newsletters at phone width (scale vs reflow), dark mode, text size, quoted-text collapsing as today, selection/copy.
- Performance with large messages, and printing/forwarding are out of scope unless you argue otherwise.
- Fixture data: the synthetic provider needs HTML samples (newsletter, tracking pixel, cid image, malicious samples) so everything can be tested without real mail.
- Validation: tests for the sanitiser with hostile inputs, browser screenshots at desktop and phone width (light and dark), Android emulator screenshots.

Report back with `ADR READY: ...` and your open questions.

input.title: Usable D: sending on macOS and Android (ADR 0006)
input.message:
You own track D of the "usable Android app" programme: sending mail, on macOS desktop and on Android (Linux and Windows desktops are out of scope: Gmail there has no token storage and stays that way). First read /home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md in full and follow it. You are in phase 1: write ADR 0006 as a proposal, push it, report `ADR READY`, and stop. Do not implement until I send GREENLIGHT.

Today there is no send path anywhere. Compose writes plain-text new messages and replies as durable local drafts that never sync to Gmail (docs/current-status.md "Composition"; DraftCore in src-tauri/src/setup.rs). Gmail scopes are read-only, with `gmail.modify` as an explicit upgrade (crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs). Mailbox writes go through an operation ledger with retry and undo, and the product rule is that pending, confirmed, failed and unknown stay distinct. Android Gmail sign-in is being designed by track B (ADR 0004); your Android part depends on it.

The ADR must cover at least:
- What "send" covers in the first version: new message and reply (plain text); reply-all, forward, Cc/Bcc, attachments, HTML composition — recommend what is in and out.
- The provider call (Gmail `messages.send` vs Gmail drafts + `drafts.send`), MIME building (headers, encoding, `In-Reply-To`/`References`/`threadId` for replies, From identity), and the `gmail.send` scope request using track B's scope-upgrade mechanism (B owns the mechanism, you own the send consent).
- Durability and honesty: an outbox through the operation ledger; what happens offline, on app kill mid-send, on timeout (unknown outcome: never send twice — idempotency/dedupe), retry, and how status is shown. Undo send (delay window) yes or no.
- What happens to the local draft after a confirmed send.
- Fixture/synthetic provider: simulated send so the whole flow is testable without Gmail, including failure and unknown-outcome injection like the existing write controls.
- UI in both layouts: the Send control in the desktop editor and the phone compose sheet (the phone editor currently exits only with X and says "never sent"; that copy must change for sendable drafts), confirmation, failure states, sent message appearing in the thread.
- Validation: unit/integration tests for MIME and the outbox state machine, browser screenshots at desktop and phone width, an Android emulator screen recording of a send in fixture mode; real-Gmail sends as an owner action.

Report back with `ADR READY: ...` and your open questions.

result.output:
# ADR 0004: Install and update Email OS on Android

**Status:** Proposed

## Context

The owner needs to install Email OS on one physical phone and update it in place
while keeping drafts, mailbox state and settings.

- `mise.toml:105–123` builds a bundled debug APK for `aarch64` and `x86_64`
  and provides a separate development run. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:9–50`
  builds and uploads a debug APK on main pushes and PRs. The Android Gradle
  project has no release signing config. Two historical CI debug artifacts had
  different certificates and Android refused the update with
  `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`. Local debug builds also use the machine's
  debug key. Uninstall removes the installed app's private data.
  [Android smoke record](../current-status.md#android-unified-fixture-smoke-2026-11-15)
- `src-tauri/tauri.android.conf.json:3` and
  `src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts:19–27` set
  `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture` as the app ID. Gradle reads version fields
  from generated `tauri.properties`, with fallbacks `1` and `1.0`. The base
  Tauri version is `0.1.0` (`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:4`). With no override, the
  pinned Tauri CLI's documented semver calculation gives code `1000` for
  `0.1.0`. Read the actual values from the archived APK before calling those
  values the historical baseline.
  [Pinned Tauri config](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.3.0/crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs#L2409-L2435)
- Gradle sets min API 24 and target API 35. Release enables R8, and resource
  shrinking is unset (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts:20–47`).
  The manifest requests `INTERNET`, uses a per-build cleartext setting, names a
  launcher icon and a non-exported FileProvider, and leaves backup at the
  platform default (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:3–36`).
  Both launcher strings say `email-os`
  (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:2–3`).
- The first cold launch after a fresh install crossed Android's reported
  5-second input-dispatch deadline waiting for a focus event. The Inbox rendered
  behind the dialog, the host was under CPU and memory pressure, and relaunch
  worked. The compact-layout check later reported the first-launch issue again.
  There is no physical-phone evidence yet. ADR 0003 covers the compact layout.
  [Android smoke record](../current-status.md#android-unified-fixture-smoke-2026-11-15)

## Options considered

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Keep debug builds and share one debug keystore | Stabilizes updates once everyone uses it, but leaves a debuggable owner app with debug cleartext policy. Switching to a new release certificate later would require another cutover. An old matching debug key could preserve one particular install, with no general solution for the other signers. |
| Sign release APKs with a new key and keep `androidfixture` | Keeps the current identifier, but existing installs signed by debug keys still require uninstall before installing the release. A later move to a final ID starts a new data sandbox and requires a new Android OAuth registration. |
| Sign release APKs with a new key and adopt a final ID now | Starts a new sandbox once, before OAuth registration and real mail. The old app can stay installed while the owner recovers anything they need. Future releases share the same application ID and certificate. |

For distribution, Actions artifacts reuse the current download path and give a
per-commit build record, with expiration and a ZIP to extract. GitHub Releases
provide a stable page and a direct APK asset, with an additional publishing step
and visibility tied to the repository. Play distribution would add store and
signing setup outside this owner's initial install path.
[Android app signing](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing)
and [GitHub artifact downloads](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/download-workflow-artifacts).

## Decision

### App identity and signing

Adopt `dev.exedev.emailos` and the launcher and activity label **Email OS** for
Android. Align the Tauri Android identifier, Gradle ID and namespace, Kotlin
package and path, generated JNI/Kotlin paths and ignore rules. The FileProvider
authority follows the application ID. The desktop identifier stays as it is.

Use a non-debuggable release APK, signed by an owner-generated, long-lived
RSA app-signing key in a password-protected JKS. The primary copy lives outside
the repository on the owner's machine. Keep an encrypted offline copy and
the passwords in the owner's password manager. Restore the backup once and
compare its certificate fingerprints before distributing the first APK. Losing
the signing key removes the ordinary in-place update path. A compromised key
allows third parties to sign APKs Android can accept as updates. Plan any
rotation against the supported Android versions and OAuth registration before
changing the signer. [Tauri Android signing](https://v2.tauri.app/distribute/sign/android/).

Gradle's release signing config reads `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH`,
`ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` and `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD`
from the process environment. The local release task uses the same config
with values supplied from the owner's password manager for one invocation.
Debug CI and local development keep ordinary debug signing for test devices.
A release request with missing or invalid key inputs fails before any artifact
is published. Do not install the debug variant over the owner app.

Use a dedicated Actions release workflow for trusted main commits. Trigger it
for an intentional version bump and allow an explicit rerun of the same version.
Restrict the `android-release` environment to main and require owner review
where supported.
Keep key inputs out of PR workflows, unreviewed refs, caches, artifacts and logs.
Decode the base64 JKS into a restricted temporary file on the hosted runner for
the signing step, disable shell tracing and remove the file on exit, including on
failure. The upload step sees only the APK and public metadata. Verify the APK
certificate against an owner-configured SHA-256 fingerprint before uploading.
Keep release signing with the owner locally if the repository cannot protect
the environment. [GitHub deployment environments](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments).

With the new ID, the old fixture APK and its data can stay on the phone alongside
Email OS. The new app starts with fresh fixture data. Copy any wanted draft text
out of the old app or keep that app installed. Automatic cross-package migration
is out of scope. The `run-as` transfer in the old smoke guide was for debuggable
test APKs. ADR 0002's same-profile legacy retirement still requires disclosure
and a verified backup, and retains local drafts.

### Versions, delivery and device support

Use the shared repository semver for `versionName` and set the Android
`bundle.android.versionCode` explicitly in the committed Android Tauri config,
starting at `1001`. In phase 2 verify the pinned CLI passes both fields into the
APK. If the CLI ignores the explicit code, have Gradle read that same committed
value. Bump the code on main for each owner-distributed revision, even when semver
stays the same. A single sequence covers CI and local builds and all ABIs.
A maintainer checks the intended code against the last owner-distributed build
before upload. Reruns of the same commit are rebuilds of that version. A rollback
ships a compatible fix at a higher code. Android's in-place update keeps app
data when the ID and signer match, the version advances, and app migrations
preserve the data. [Android versioning](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning).

Start with one universal signed release APK for `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64`, named
`email-os-android-release.apk` in a versioned Actions artifact. The owner downloads
and unzips it from the approved run, or uses `gh run download` with the run ID
and artifact name. Record the commit, versions, file size, APK SHA-256 and
certificate fingerprints. The owner can retain the APK after artifact expiry.
Revisit GitHub Releases if a durable direct download becomes necessary.

Keep R8 and start with resource shrinking off. Verify that the minified
release's JNI, WebView and IPC work on both ABIs before considering additional
shrinking. Measure the signed universal APK and the contribution of each
native library using APK Analyzer or ZIP entries. There is no measured release
size yet. If download or storage size is a problem, measure an ARM64-only APK
and consider per-ABI output with the same ID, signer and version sequence.
Check APK ZIP alignment with `zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4 <apk>` and ELF LOAD segment
alignment of each packaged shared library. If the pinned NDK r27 produces
unaligned segments, use Android's documented linker flags and retest. Run on
a 16 KB device or image if available and record the actual coverage. ARM64 is
the expected phone ABI. The initial APK omits 32-bit libraries.
[Android 16 KB page size guidance](https://developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes).

### First-launch ANR

`src-tauri/src/setup.rs:40–76` performs profile open synchronously inside the
Tauri setup callback. `open_fixture_core` resolves the fixture profile
(`setup.rs:17–26`). The synthetic open takes the profile lock, creates or opens
the synthetic provider's facts DB, then opens the Gmail store and preloads the
synthetic mailbox before the worker starts
(`crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs:341–360,423–444,1920–1960`). The fact store
migrates and seeds with WAL and full synchronous durability
(`crates/mail-core/src/synthetic/facts.rs:39–58`). Draft open takes its own
lock, opens SQLite and runs schema setup
(`crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs:37–69`). These steps cost more on a new
profile and under I/O or scheduling pressure.

Constructing `FixtureTransition` merely records the directory
(`crates/mail-core/src/fixture_transition.rs:225–245`). The Vue gate loads
status after mount, and the status and accept commands already use
`spawn_blocking` (`src/components/FixtureTransitionGate.vue:34–51`,
`src-tauri/src/commands/transition.rs:7–24`). Status checks markers and can
finish a previously accepted reset, while a fresh profile has no legacy
database to back up (`fixture_transition.rs:247–279,342–386`). The bundled
frontend mounts `StartupRoot` (`src/main.ts:17–22`), then mounts `App` once the
gate clears (`src/StartupRoot.vue:12–21`). The mailbox then subscribes, loads
account status and loads the list
(`src/composables/useMailbox.ts:805–828,1185–1187`).

The leading hypothesis is that fresh SQLite setup and synthetic preload delay
native readiness or event handling alongside first-use WebView work. Source
inspection puts the Tauri callback on the Rust/Tao event loop. The timeout is
for an Android Activity focus event, so the finding alone cannot establish
that SQLite blocked the Android UI thread. A platform WebView stall or emulator
scheduling starvation could also explain it. The legacy backup path is a low
priority suspect on empty installs.

After approval, time Activity creation (including `super.onCreate`), WebView
creation, first frame and focus callback, Rust setup and each profile-open
phase, transition IPC and Vue first paint and Inbox ready. Log only stage,
thread and monotonic durations, with no mailbox data or request payloads.
Compare first launches of fresh installs and process-cold launches of populated
profiles on the same emulator, in quiet and representative load, then use the
ARM64 phone. If it recurs, capture timestamped logcat, an ANR main-thread stack
and a Perfetto scheduler/I/O trace on the test device. Use the thread stacks
and wait chain to distinguish blocked native work, WebView startup and CPU
starvation. Compare against an otherwise equivalent diagnostic build that
moves profile I/O off the event loop.
[Android ANR diagnosis](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/anrs/diagnose-and-fix-anrs).

If profile open is on the critical path, move Android's blocking profile work
to one background task. Show a focusable startup surface immediately. Register
the readiness gate before any page IPC. Make the transition and mailbox UI wait
asynchronously for one complete state, with a recoverable error state and a
serialized retry after partial resources are released. Keep the legacy
disclosure gate before mailbox access, the single-writer profile locks, and
the existing startup recovery rules. Exercise a deliberately delayed and a
failed open. If the trace instead implicates Activity or WebView startup,
address that path and measure again. A branded splash alone cannot fix an
input timeout.

### Manifest and presentation

Keep the normal `INTERNET` permission. Fixture launch works offline and needs
no runtime permission prompts. Mail profiles stay in app-private storage.
No broad storage permission is needed. Check the merged manifest for additional
permissions or exported components, and keep the FileProvider internal with
grants limited to the intended files if a later feature needs it.

Set `allowBackup=false` and explicit exclusion rules for cloud and
device-to-device transfer on API 31+, with full-backup exclusions on older
versions. Cover app storage including the profiles, SQLite side files,
WebView state and future credential material. Some manufacturers can still run
device transfer with `allowBackup=false` alone. Backup settings do not affect
in-place updates. Clearing storage, uninstalling or changing phones can lose
local drafts. [Android Auto Backup](https://developer.android.com/identity/data/autobackup).

Keep release cleartext disabled and the bundled Tauri WebView and IPC working.
Use platform-trusted HTTPS for later Gmail and send paths. If a track needs
Android Network Security Config for a documented debug-only endpoint, keep the
exception in the debug variant and test the signed release's effective policy.
Validate TLS trust separately in the Rust HTTP client, which uses rustls
(`crates/mail-core/Cargo.toml:20`), since manifest settings alone do not
configure that client. Retain the WebView CSP and avoid broadening it for
native API calls. [Android network security configuration](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/security-config).

Verify the launcher art from the repository at phone sizes, with an adaptive
icon and a legacy fallback where needed. Use the Email OS icon and matching
window background for the system splash, and check handoff to the app in
light and dark mode, including Android 12+. Keep the compact layout, safe
insets, soft keyboard resizing and Back behavior from ADR 0003.

## Scope and out of scope

Scope covers APK packaging and signing, application identity, update delivery,
first-launch diagnostics and repair, the Android manifest and resources, and
emulator and owner phone verification. Store distribution, an in-app updater,
automatic old-package migration, and device-to-device restore are outside this
proposal. Tracks B, C and D own Google sign-in, HTML mail and sending.

## Owner actions

1. After approval and before the first signed build, confirm the app ID and
   create the key on the owner's machine. Use an interactive command so key
   passwords are prompted and stay out of shell history.

   ```sh
   umask 077
   mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/email-os/signing"
   keytool -genkeypair -storetype JKS -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 \
     -keystore "$HOME/.local/share/email-os/signing/email-os-release.jks" \
     -alias email-os-release
   keytool -list -v -storetype JKS \
     -keystore "$HOME/.local/share/email-os/signing/email-os-release.jks" \
     -alias email-os-release
   ```

   Store the encrypted backup and passwords, verify the restored certificate, and
   share only the SHA-1 and SHA-256 certificate fingerprints for verification
   and OAuth registration.
2. Once the signing workflow is reviewed, open repository **Settings →
   Environments → android-release** and restrict deployment branches. Add
   environment secrets `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` (the single-line base64 JKS),
   `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`, and `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD`.
   Set the environment variable `ANDROID_RELEASE_CERT_SHA256` to the public
   certificate digest from `keytool`. Base64 is reversible. Put it directly in
   the secret field, and keep the JKS and passwords off the shared VM and out of
   messages. For pre-merge CI validation, temporarily allow a protected candidate
   branch only if the owner can review the exact workflow and candidate commit
   before granting secret access. Remove that branch from the environment when
   the test is done. Otherwise use two owner-local signed candidates before
   merge, then compare the first trusted CI build after merge. Use main for
   routine builds.
3. Before starting the phone test, report device model and Android version, and
   whether the old fixture app has any drafts to keep. Perform the phone steps
   below using two approved signed versions. If Android blocks direct APK
   install, record the exact message and report whether USB/ADB is available.
   If developer verification becomes required for this install route, the
   owner handles registration for the final ID and signing certificate.
   [Android developer verification rollout](https://developer.android.com/developer-verification).

## Dependencies

- **Track B (ADR 0005)** needs the approved application ID early and the
  release signing certificate SHA-1 as soon as the owner generates the key.
  Track A verifies that SHA-1 against the signed APK with
  `apksigner verify --verbose --print-certs`. Track B owns the Android OAuth
  client registration with the owner, its callback, and token storage. A
  debug signer needs a separate OAuth registration if B chooses to use one.
  B should use the startup readiness contract if the Android profile changes.
  [Google Android OAuth credentials](https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials#android).
- **Track C (ADR 0006)** can use the signed fixture APK for native reader checks.
  Its HTML resource policy stays within its own design.
- **Track D (ADR 0007)** gets the same signed install/update path and network
  baseline. D owns sending permissions, endpoint and TLS requirements and
  delegates any manifest or network-policy dependency back to A for review.

## Implementation plan

All stages start after GREENLIGHT. Use the programme's shared Rust build settings,
single-heavy-job rule and emulator lock.

1. **Identity and release build.** Align Android IDs and label, wire signed
   release packaging and the version source, and keep debug CI. Follow the
   programme's generated-source preparation for a legacy baseline build.
   Regenerate Wry/Tauri output for the new package and verify JNI names and
   ignore rules. Use a clean CI checkout to check generation if the shared
   build cache skips it. Check the finished APK with `aapt dump badging` and
   `apksigner verify --verbose --print-certs`, inspect both ABIs and alignment,
   and verify a release request without signing inputs fails. The owner runs
   the local production-key signing check, while development checks can use a
   throwaway key on synthetic test installs.
2. **Startup diagnosis.** Add temporary timing markers and capture baseline
   cold-start timing for empty and populated profiles on the shared emulator.
   Check for a correlated main-thread stack if the timeout recurs and document
   where time was spent.
3. **Startup repair.** Change the path identified in stage 2. If moving profile
   open, check delayed readiness, typed failure and retry, single-writer
   exclusion and the ADR 0002 disclosure, cancel and recovery cases. Compare the
   before and after cold-start timing and record the startup flow.
4. **Manifest and launcher.** Add the backup policy and validate the packaged
   release manifest, release/debug networking, and bundled offline boot. Check
   launcher, splash, Inbox and keyboard screenshots for label, clipping, insets
   and first-frame continuity.
5. **Trusted delivery and update.** Add Actions signing and verified artifact
   upload. Verify artifact contents and cert digest, then exercise the emulator
   and owner's phone update flows below. Record versions and hashes, APK size,
   and the install and persistence results. Update the development and current
   status guides with the working path.

## Validation plan

### Automated and browser

- Run `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`,
  including the core fixture transition and profile-lock tests and shell
  startup and draft bridge tests. Run
  `pnpm exec vitest run tests/transition/gate.test.ts tests/layout/mobile-android-back.test.ts`
  for the frontend gate and Android-related regressions. If startup readiness
  changes, add focused cases for failure, retry and delayed availability.
- Use the programme Chromium binary to run `mise run test:rendered` and
  `mise run screenshots:mobile` with `EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR` pointing at the
  evidence directory. Review compact Inbox and compose and capture the startup
  surface through a rendered test harness if it changes. Browser evidence
  covers the shared layout, and Android evidence covers native startup.

### Android emulator

- Use the programme lock and T3 device tools on `local/emulator-5554`.
  Preserve any existing test state. Install version N of the universal release,
  then version N+1 via `adb install -r <apk>` without uninstalling N. Prefer
  owner-local N and trusted CI N+1 signed by the same key when available.
  Confirm both versions with APK metadata and verify both certs. Use disposable
  synthetic builds for a wrong-signer negative check and a legacy transition
  regression. The production release need not support `run-as`.
- Repeat at least five first launches with empty test data and five
  process-cold launches with populated test data before and after the startup
  change. Include quiet and representative emulator load. Record timings for
  first frame/focus and Inbox ready, plus Android version, WebView version,
  load and any ANR. The launch path should accept Back or Home while
  initialization is deliberately delayed. An observed ANR blocks acceptance.
- Before the update, save a synthetic draft, mark a specific conversation done
  and change a swipe setting. After the update, verify the exact draft fields,
  the same conversation in Done and the saved setting. Relaunch and repeat.
  Check reader, IME resize, Back, background/resume and offline launch.
  Capture launcher, startup, Inbox and retained draft screenshots and
  short fresh-launch and update/reopen recordings (each at most 60 seconds).
  Use `docs/validation/android-install/` for small synthetic evidence and
  `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/android-install/` for larger videos and traces.
  Release the lock and restore the emulator's original settings.

### Owner's physical phone

1. Keep any existing fixture install. In **Settings → About phone**, note the
   model and Android version. Use a device on Android 7 or later with an ABI
   in the artifact. If the ABI or page size needs confirmation and USB
   debugging is available, check `adb shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abilist`
   and `adb shell getconf PAGE_SIZE` from the owner's computer.
2. On the phone, sign in to GitHub if required, open the provided Actions run,
   download the approved version N artifact and unzip it in Files. Open
   `email-os-android-release.apk`. If prompted, allow installs from this source
   for Files (or the app opening the APK), then tap **Install**. If local
   signing is used, copy the verified APK to Downloads first. If the direct
   install is blocked and the device allows USB debugging, use
   `adb install <version-N.apk>` after authorizing the computer prompt.
3. Tap **Open** immediately and note time to Inbox, any blank screen, slow
   focus or system dialog. Open a conversation. In a new draft enter
   `install-check@example.test`, subject `Android update check`, and body
   `Keep this draft across the update.` Wait for the local save confirmation.
   Mark a known fixture conversation done and change a swipe setting.
   Background and reopen Email OS. Force stop it in Android App info,
   then open from the launcher and confirm the draft, Done and setting.
4. Download and unzip the approved N+1 artifact in the same way. Open the APK
   and tap **Update** (or use `adb install -r <version-N+1.apk>`). If Android
   rejects the update, keep the app installed and report the exact error.
   After success, verify the displayed version if changed (or use the APK
   metadata and installer result), reopen Drafts and check the exact text,
   check Done and the swipe setting, and repeat after force stop. Turn on
   Airplane mode, open the fixture Inbox and draft, then restore connectivity.
   Revoke the temporary Files install permission or disable USB debugging if
   enabled only for this test.
5. Report device and Android version, the two build codes, install/update
   results, time/behavior at first launch and whether the draft, Done and
   setting survived. Use screenshots or video with synthetic data only.

## Risks and open questions

- Approve `dev.exedev.emailos` as the long-lived Android ID. Does an existing
  fixture install hold drafts the owner needs to keep?
- Can the owner hold and back up the release key, and can the repository use
  an owner-reviewed signing environment? Confirm whether access-controlled
  Actions downloads meet the owner's delivery needs and who can access them.
- Which phone model and Android version will be used, and can the owner run
  the two-version update test? Sideloading support depends on device policy.
  Record installation friction even if ADB works.
- The ANR mechanism, signed APK size and 16 KB runtime coverage remain to be
  measured. Report the observed results and the device coverage before
  recommending the APK for daily use.

input.message:
Coordinator review of ADR 0004 @ 3ae2a80. Good proposal; the ANR investigation plan and backup policy are right. Please revise these points, push, and report `ADR READY` again. Do not implement yet.

1. versionCode must not depend on a person remembering to bump it (a forgotten bump makes Android refuse the update as a downgrade or same-version). Make it automatic for owner builds: e.g. the release workflow is `workflow_dispatch` on main only and sets versionCode from a monotonic source (`1000 + github.run_number`, or commit count on main), passed into the build; local release builds need an explicit override and are for emergencies only. Pick one and justify it. versionName stays the repo semver.
2. Phase 2 must be finishable and verifiable without the owner's key. Drop the "temporarily allow a protected candidate branch" step. Instead: prove the release pipeline in PR CI with an ephemeral throwaway key generated inside the job (artifact not published, or clearly named as unsigned-for-distribution), and do the emulator N → N+1 update test locally with a throwaway key. The first owner-key build is an owner action after merge, with exact steps.
3. The repository is PUBLIC (`gh repo view` says so). Say what that means: Actions artifacts and release assets are downloadable by any signed-in GitHub user (fine: the APK holds no secrets, and track B's Android OAuth client id is not a secret), and environment protection rules with required reviewers are available on public repos. Make sure no workflow path can expose the keystore to PR runs from forks.
4. Stage 1's package rename moves `src-tauri/gen/android/.../androidfixture/...`. Track B will add Android-native code there later. State in Dependencies that A's rename lands first and B builds on it.
5. Keep launcher/splash work minimal (label, adaptive icon from existing art, no new artwork).

Open owner questions (package ID `dev.exedev.emailos`, phone model/Android version, key custody, Actions artifacts vs Releases) are mine to ask; I'll collect them across all four ADRs. Leave them in the ADR's open-questions section.
