# ADR 0007: Send plain-text mail on macOS and Android

**Status:** Proposed

## Context

- New messages and replies are plain-text local drafts with no send path
  ([docs/current-status.md:13](../current-status.md#runtime-availability)).
  The shell opens a separate draft database for the selected profile
  ([src-tauri/src/setup.rs:62](../../src-tauri/src/setup.rs#L62)).
  Draft saves and deletes use revision checks and durable request receipts
  ([crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs:228](../../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs#L228)).
  Disconnect retains local drafts while clearing the Gmail cache and mailbox
  operation history ([crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/profile.rs:301](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/profile.rs#L301)).
- Reply preparation already checks the displayed source, selects validated
  Reply-To or From mailboxes, and persists the source Message-ID and References
  alongside the conversation ID
  ([crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs:540](../../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs#L540)).
  The draft model includes editable To, Cc and Subject fields
  ([crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs:35](../../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs#L35)).
- Gmail starts with `gmail.readonly` and requests `gmail.modify` through a
  separate mailbox-actions upgrade
  ([crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs:26](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs#L26)).
  macOS uses Keychain, and the existing Keychain adapter fails closed on other
  platforms ([crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs:84](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs#L84)).
  Android currently selects fixture mode
  ([src-tauri/src/setup.rs:40](../../src-tauri/src/setup.rs#L40)).
- The ledger returns acceptance receipts after persistence and claims work before
  provider calls. Interrupted applying rows become outcome-unknown
  ([crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/worker.rs:4](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/worker.rs#L4),
  [crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/profile.rs:30](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store/profile.rs#L30)).
  The current worker executes label setters. Its synthetic policy can requeue an
  interrupted setter whose intended state is absent
  ([crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs:160](../../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs#L160)).
- The shared editor footer has Save and close on desktop and the compact sheets
  use a header X. The editor describes drafts as “never sent”
  ([src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue:101](../../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue#L101),
  [src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue:366](../../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue#L366),
  [src/components/ComposeCard.vue:120](../../src/components/ComposeCard.vue#L120),
  [src/components/ReplyComposer.vue:132](../../src/components/ReplyComposer.vue#L132)).
  ADR 0003 established these layouts. ADR 0002 established the shared synthetic
  provider seam.

## Options considered

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Send the local draft via `users.messages.send` | One provider write and the narrow `gmail.send` scope. The API exposes no idempotency key. A lost response needs read-only reconciliation and can remain unresolved. |
| Create a Gmail draft, then use `users.drafts.send` | The stable draft ID provides another recovery clue, and a successful send consumes the draft. This also creates a remote draft visible to other clients, requires a broader compose-capable scope, and adds a create request whose own result can be lost. A missing draft can also mean deletion. |
| Send directly from the editor and wait for HTTP | Smaller initial change. Offline sends have to wait in the editor, and a lost IPC response or process exit leaves the app without a durable record of whether it already attempted the send. |
| Queue in the operation ledger | Recovers the user's intent and the dispatch state independently of the editor. Requires an atomic handoff from the saved draft and separate retry rules for an irreversible operation. |

[Gmail send endpoint](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages/send),
[Gmail drafts lifecycle](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/drafts),
[Gmail draft send endpoint](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.drafts/send).

## Decision (proposed)

Use `users.messages.send` with an immutable send intent in the operation ledger.
It preserves local draft ownership, requires only one sending write, and lets the
same core enforce the recovery rules on both platforms and in fixture mode.

### Consent and identity

Keep initial sign-in read-only. **Enable sending** explains that the app will be
allowed to send mail from the connected address. Use track B's same-account
scope-upgrade mechanism to request
`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send` alongside the existing access.
Track D owns the disclosure, trigger and send capability. Track B owns OAuth,
scope verification, refresh and secure credential storage. Require a verified
send grant and explicit send enablement for that account. An existing
`gmail.modify` grant is sufficient at the endpoint but does not enable sending
in the app. Verify with track B that the upgrade can return a usable send grant
for an account that already has modify access without dropping its existing
read and mailbox-action access. Missing, denied or cancelled consent preserves
the draft and prior access. Returning from consent never queues a draft.
Recheck account identity and the grant immediately before dispatch. Loss of
permission pauses queued sends until the same account restores access and
explicitly resumes. Fixture mode exposes send capability without consent or
credentials. [Gmail scope reference](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes).

### MIME and replies

- Build MIME in Rust with a standards-aware serializer and structured header
  values. Emit From, To, Cc when present, Subject, Date, Message-ID and
  MIME-Version. From is the verified primary mailbox of the active account
  (the fixture identity in fixture mode). Omit an editable From and alias
  selection. Use a single `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` part with base64 transfer
  encoding. Encode non-ASCII subjects as RFC 2047 encoded words, fold headers
  at legal boundaries, use CRLF framing and base64url-encode the complete MIME
  for the JSON `raw` field. Generate a random RFC Message-ID and fix the Date
  at acceptance. Persist both through retries of the same intent.
- Validate again in core at send time. Accept comma-separated, bare ASCII
  mailboxes with at least one To and at most 20 distinct recipients in To and
  Cc combined, using the existing reply mailbox validation rules. Flag duplicates
  so the confirmation shows the actual envelope. Reject controls in headers,
  invalid addresses and oversized input under the existing draft bounds.
  Preserve Unicode and line breaks in the body. Local saves can still hold
  incomplete editor text. Show an empty subject explicitly in confirmation.
- For a reply, use the persisted, account-bound reply link for the exact
  source the user chose. Set `In-Reply-To` to the source RFC Message-ID and
  `References` to the validated chain ending in that ID. Supply the provider
  conversation ID as JSON `threadId`. Persist the source subject when
  preparing new reply drafts and allow the normal `Re:` prefix. For an older
  draft without that subject, verify it against exact-source metadata on
  demand and leave the draft editable if the read is unavailable. A missing
  or invalid link or a mismatched subject blocks threaded send and offers a
  deliberate Save as new. A newer message arriving
  in the thread does not retarget an existing reply. Use the provider's
  returned thread ID if it differs from the requested one.
  [Internet Message Format](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5322),
  [Gmail threading requirements](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages#Message).

### Outbox, recovery and draft lifecycle

Use the existing account-scoped ledger and serial worker, with a distinct send
operation and payload. Send does not enter label preimages, group actions or
Undo selection. Put send-capable draft rows, revision receipts and tombstones in
the same profile SQLite transaction boundary as the ledger. Under the profile
lock, import existing `local-drafts/drafts.db` rows and request receipts with
IDs, revisions, content and reply links intact. Record the import marker in the
same transaction. A failed import leaves the source intact and a restart after
commit never imports it again. Retire the old draft store only after a verified
commit. Preserve the existing durability settings and fixture transition.

Send confirmation flushes the editor and submits a request ID, DraftRef and
expected revision. In one transaction check account, revision and eligibility,
persist the frozen MIME and original request receipt, and lock the draft
against edit, discard or another live send. Replaying the same account and
request ID with the same arguments returns the original receipt even after
confirmation. Changed arguments conflict. A second request ID cannot claim a
draft already locked by pending or unknown work. The worker checks the session
generation and uses the same-account credential for dispatch. Nothing holds a
database transaction open across provider I/O.

| Ledger state | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Pending, queued | The accepted draft is durable. The worker waits for connectivity and same-account access, then sends while the app is running. Preflight errors known to precede dispatch leave it queued with a status reason and backoff. **Cancel queued send** restores the editable draft and atomically wins or loses against the dispatch claim. There is no timed delay or Undo Send. |
| Pending, applying | Commit an applying marker immediately before the first possible POST. Stop accepting cancellation of the send once this marker commits. Disable transport-level redirects and POST retries for this endpoint. Process exit before the marker leaves a queued intent. Exit after the marker, including after provider acceptance but before local confirmation commits, recovers as unknown. |
| Confirmed | A valid successful send response with authoritative message and thread IDs, or positive Sent evidence, confirms provider acceptance for sending. In the same commit, persist those IDs, delete the draft with a tombstone, and remove the frozen payload. The receipt remains queryable after cleanup. “Sent” reports provider acceptance. Recipient delivery is outside the app's evidence. |
| Failed | A documented, definitive provider refusal or an unrecoverable pre-dispatch validation failure leaves the draft intact and editable. For a retryable refusal, an unchanged revision can be retried explicitly from the latest failed attempt with a new request ID and a link to that attempt, reusing the frozen identity and MIME. Editing the draft invalidates the old retry and requires new confirmation. |
| Outcome unknown | A transport failure after dispatch becomes possible, an ambiguous response (including a 5xx or unusable success receipt), or an interrupted applying row takes this path. Keep the draft available read-only with the original intent. Neither the worker, a reconnect, nor a generic Activity Retry can POST it again. Later operations can continue. |
| Cancelled before dispatch | Retain the receipt, release the draft and discard the frozen payload. A later send requires a new confirmation and request ID. |

Retire a failed attempt's frozen payload when an edit, discard or newer
attempt supersedes its retry. Keep MIME, addresses, provider response bodies
and credentials out of routine diagnostics.

For an unknown send, check the expected reply thread and use bounded, paced Sent
lookup by `rfc822msgid:` on startup or a sync beat and via **Check status**. Use
the existing read access to fetch a candidate and verify its exact Message-ID,
Sent label and sender in the active account. Require an unambiguous positive
match. No match, incomplete results or a rewritten Message-ID leave the outcome
unknown. The generated ID correlates observations and does not make Gmail's POST
idempotent. The guarantee is no automatic or manual replay of that uncertain
intent, including in fixture mode. A deliberately composed separate message is
a separate intent. [Gmail search API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages/list),
[Gmail error guidance](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/handle-errors).

Disconnect cancels work still queued at the dispatch barrier and restores those
drafts. Work that crossed the barrier remains confirmed or unknown according to
the available evidence. Keep account-scoped local draft locks and minimal send
receipts needed to recover unknown or confirmed sends across same-account
reconnect. Other accounts see none of them. Update disconnect copy to explain
that queued sends are cancelled and that a send already started may have gone
through. Continue clearing credentials and the ordinary cache on disconnect.

### Editors, Activity and the reader

- Place **Send** in the shared desktop editor footer and in the compact compose
  sheet header beside X for both new messages and replies. Keep X and Escape
  as save-and-close actions. Replace blanket “never sent” copy on send-capable
  surfaces with “Local draft” or “Saved on this device.” Keep the Send target
  reachable with the keyboard open. Enter in any editor field does not send.
- Open an accessible confirmation showing the verified From, every To/Cc and
  the subject of the saved revision. Cancel returns focus to the editor.
  A concurrent edit invalidates confirmation. Disable duplicate submission and
  recover an interrupted IPC response by replaying the same request ID.
  Close the editor after durable acceptance and announce “Queued to send.”
- Use an Outbox section in Activity in both layouts, with persistent rows and
  short status copy. Show “Queued to send,” “Sending…,” “Sent,” “Send failed,”
  or “Send outcome unknown,” with a reason/action as appropriate. A failed
  draft is available to reopen. Unknown shows Check status and explains that
  the message may already have been sent. Drafts directs pending and unknown
  items to their outbox status rather than to an editable composer.
- After confirmation, fetch the exact returned thread through the account-fenced
  read path. Merge provider messages by provider message ID and invalidate
  reader detail/visible destination snapshots so the sent reply appears once
  without stealing focus. Give confirmed new messages an **Open conversation**
  action in Activity that can fetch sent-only threads outside Inbox discovery.
  Refresh failure leaves the send confirmed and the thread refresh retryable.
  Pending and unknown sends do not render an outgoing message as sent.

### Synthetic provider and browser fake

Use the same ledger, MIME and worker in native fixture mode. The synthetic
provider persists a Sent message on the requested thread or creates a new
thread without Inbox membership, and returns synthetic provider IDs. Use its
existing pause and one-shot rejection controls
([crates/mail-core/src/synthetic/provider.rs:35](../../crates/mail-core/src/synthetic/provider.rs#L35)).
Extend them with fixture-only one-shot outcomes for commit-then-lose-response
and lose-response-without-commit, with controllable Sent visibility for tests.
Keep scripted barriers in test support and make the fixed outcomes available
for manual fixture validation without credentials. The browser fake models the
same observable states and controls in memory.

## Scope and out of scope

Include new messages and replies with plain-text bodies, To and editable Cc,
on macOS and Android in fixture and supported Gmail profiles. Sending a reply
uses the existing Reply-To or From defaults. The browser fake supports UI
validation with synthetic data.

Defer reply-all, forward, Bcc, attachments, HTML composition, alias selection,
provider-synced drafts, scheduled send, Undo Send and sending while the app is
fully quit. Linux and Windows desktop send and Gmail token storage are outside
this proposal. Keep the send capability unavailable on those native platforms.

## Owner actions

1. Before live consent validation, use the Google Cloud project that owns the
   existing macOS OAuth client and track B's Android configuration. Add
   `gmail.send` to the consent configuration for that project and make the
   disposable sender eligible for the applicable testing audience. Keep existing
   client configuration and secrets in their approved local channels. Before
   public distribution, confirm the project's verification requirements for the
   scopes used. [Google OAuth and scope requirements](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes).
2. After fixture validation and after track B can authenticate the approved
   Android build, the owner runs real sends on macOS and Android. Use a
   disposable sender and a recipient inbox the owner controls. Exercise
   deny/cancel, grant and return to the draft, a new send and a threaded reply.
   Verify From, To/Cc as applicable, Unicode content, one message per attempt,
   provider Sent, recipient receipt and thread placement. Record observations
   without committing real addresses, message content or credentials.

## Dependencies

- **Track B, ADR 0005.** Needs to expose a reusable same-account scope upgrade
  and verified grants on macOS and Android, plus the appropriate refresh and
  disconnect fences. Track D supplies the exact send scope, disclosure and
  capability contract, including the existing-modify case. Fixture send and
  core tests can proceed independently of the live Android integration.
- **Track A, ADR 0004.** Supplies the installable Android build lane and the
  approved package/signing configuration used for the owner run. Track D
  supplies the send smoke steps and fixture evidence. Coordinate shared
  emulator use under the programme lock.
- **Track C, ADR 0006.** Plain-text sends use the existing renderer and the
  provider-observed reader model. Share the thread invalidation expectations
  with C so that a sent reply refreshes the same reader.

## Implementation plan

1. Add core send validation and MIME construction with an independent parse
   round-trip. Check focused MIME tests for Unicode, folding, body limits,
   injection, Reply-To-derived recipients, Cc and thread headers.
2. Put drafts and send admission in one profile transaction boundary, initially
   with the capability disabled. Check legacy import/reopen, failure before and
   after the import commit, and preservation of draft reply links and receipts.
3. Add send-specific claim, cancellation, completion and retry to the ledger.
   Check restart, concurrent claim/cancel, lost acceptance ACK, edits after
   failure, confirmed cleanup and the disconnect/account fences with a stub
   provider.
4. Implement the synthetic provider and fixed fault controls. Check native
   fixture integration through send, provider reopen, one-row thread projection,
   both unknown paths and exactly one invocation for a lost response.
5. Wire the bridge, generated IPC contract and in-memory fake. Check
   `mise run check:contract`, native bridge tests, and fake-client parity for
   pending, failed, confirmed and unknown. Keep live Gmail sending gated.
6. Wire the shared editor, confirmation, Activity and confirmed-thread refresh.
   Check component tests for draft flush and conflict, focus, permission return,
   failure and unknown copy, and rendered composer behavior at both widths.
7. Wire live Gmail send, targeted reads and consent against B's contract.
   Check mock HTTP requests, scopes, account verification, response boundaries,
   positive-only reconciliation, and the absence of POST retries. Keep the
   real-Gmail validation owner-run.

## Validation plan

- Run the focused MIME, migration, ledger and provider tests above. Cover
  malformed/empty address inputs, Unicode text, single-level Re threading,
  valid and invalid grants, denied consent, offline/reconnect, crash before
  and after dispatch, a lost IPC receipt, 5xx/timeout, delayed Sent visibility,
  missing evidence, repeated status checks, and stable provider-call counts.
  Test an archive/Undo alongside sending to check the existing ledger behavior.
  Run `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`
  and the rendered suites using the programme's shared build limits.
- Capture Chromium screenshots at desktop and phone widths using the
  repository's rendered screenshot harness and the configured
  `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME`. Capture both editors, confirmation,
  queued/failed/unknown Activity, and the confirmed reply in the thread. Use
  `mise run screenshots:mobile` for phone evidence and the rendered editor
  suite with a desktop viewport for desktop evidence.
- Under the emulator lock, use the T3 device session to capture Android fixture
  screenshots including the open keyboard, confirmation, Outbox status and
  reader. Record a fixture send from compose through confirmation to one sent
  message in the reader (`agent-device record`, at most 60 seconds). Exercise
  offline queue/restart and the two fault paths separately. Store small
  synthetic artifacts in `docs/validation/send/` and list larger video paths
  from `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/send/` in the PR.
- Record owner-only live results separately from fixture and mocked HTTP
  evidence. Include macOS Keychain and Android credential reuse across restart
  in the live check.

## Risks and open questions

- Gmail can accept a message before the app commits the receipt. Sent lookup
  can lag or fail to match the generated Message-ID. Approve leaving such an
  intent read-only and unknown indefinitely when positive evidence is absent?
- Approve manual Cc in the first release using the existing field, with Bcc
  deferred, and require changed-subject replies to be sent as new drafts?
- Can track B expose an explicit `gmail.send` grant for accounts already
  authorized for `gmail.modify` on both clients? Verify with the owner's test
  project before exposing live send to that account state.

content.text: ADR 0007 (sending) is in: careful and thorough. Sending the technical comments now; the product questions go to you once all four are in.

input.message:
Coordinator review of ADR 0007 @ b0f4171. Strong proposal: `messages.send` + immutable ledger intent + positive-evidence-only reconciliation + no replay is the right core. Revise these points, push, and report `ADR READY` again. Do not implement yet.

1. Stage 2 (moving drafts into the profile DB with an import) is the riskiest part: it migrates the user's drafts to enable a lock. Compare it honestly against keeping `local-drafts` separate with the ledger as the single source of truth: the send intent carries the frozen MIME, draft id and revision; the draft store gets a "locked by send op X" mark; startup reconciles both directions from the ledger (confirmed → delete draft, cancelled/failed → unlock, mark without a ledger row → unlock). Name a concrete failure that the separate-store design cannot handle; if you cannot, choose the smaller design.
2. Unknown outcome: keep "no automatic or manual replay of that intent", but give the user a way out: an explicit "Copy to a new draft" action on an unknown row that creates a separate editable draft (a new intent if sent), with copy that says the first one may already have been sent. Unknown rows stay until positive evidence or the user dismisses them.
3. Changed-subject replies: don't force "Save as new". Gmail only honours `threadId` when the subject matches; if the user changed the subject beyond a `Re:` prefix, send without `threadId` but keep `In-Reply-To`/`References`, and say in the editor that it will start a new conversation. Recommend that unless you see a correctness problem.
4. The send-confirmation dialog on every send and the size of the Activity "Outbox" UI are product questions I'm taking to the owner (their earlier rule: endings stay quiet, no countdowns, no "Moved to Done" toasts). Write the ADR so both are a clear owner decision: option A, a confirmation sheet on every send; option B, no dialog, recipients always visible in the editor, Send acts at once, with status only in Drafts/Activity. Mark your recommendation.
5. Implementation plan: say which stages finish without track B (stages 1–6 plus fixture Android) and which wait for B's merged scope-upgrade mechanism (7), so I can schedule D before B lands.

Answers to your open questions: Cc yes (existing field), Bcc deferred, see point 3 for subjects, and for B's mechanism: B will be told to support adding `gmail.send` to an account that already has modify, on both platforms.

It is pushed to `usable/android-gmail` with status Proposed. Nothing is implemented and nothing was built.

**What the ADR proposes:**
- **Sign-in:** Google's Android sign-in service on the phone, part of Google Play services. Consent is Google's own system screen. Each Google Cloud "Android" client is tied to the package name and the SHA-1 fingerprint of one signing key from track A. No client id or secret goes into the build; Google matches the app by package name and signing key.
  - I rejected reusing the desktop browser-redirect flow, because Google has moved phones off it.
  - The other option, a browser tab that redirects back through a custom URL scheme, is kept as a fallback. Google now turns that scheme off by default for Android clients and says it may remove it.
- **Reuse of the Rust code:** everything above the access token is reused: the Gmail HTTP calls, account binding, scope checks, sync and the operation ledger. The PKCE, code-exchange and refresh code is not used on Android; it moves behind a new seam in `mail-core`. A fake behind that seam lets the whole Android path be tested on Linux.
- **Token storage:** the phone never holds a refresh token. The access token lives only in memory. The stored record holds no token, only the account, address and granted scopes. It is encrypted with an Android Keystore key and kept in `noBackupFilesDir`. Any failure shows the existing `SecretsUnavailable` error; there is no plaintext fallback. App backup is turned off.
- **Switching modes:** a `mode.json` file plus an in-app swap. On first run a choice screen offers your own mail or the demo mailbox. The Account page has **Use your own mail** and **Switch to demo mailbox**. Switching to the demo does not disconnect Gmail. Disconnect clears the account locally, as on desktop. The fixture becomes the labelled demo mailbox, unchanged.
- **Scopes:** granted scopes become a set. A single `request_grant(GmailGrant)` call always asks for what is already granted plus the new scope. Track D adds a `Send` value and owns its consent, UI and command. Google's `gmail.modify` scope already allows sending, so whether D asks for `gmail.send` separately is D's call.
- **Network and background:** sync runs only while the app is open. It pauses when the app goes to the background and runs once on resume. When the network comes back, one sync runs straight away. There is no background service, WorkManager or push.
- **Android gates:** saving attachments and opening links stay off. Links belong to track C. Account, sync, upgrade and mailbox actions work on Android in Gmail mode.
- **Owner actions:** the ADR lists exact Google Cloud console steps, the test-user setup and the evidence plan. Some evidence needs no Google account; the rest needs one.

**Risks:**
- The shared emulator's Play services cannot be updated, because its image has no Play Store. If its version is too old for the sign-in API, the real sign-in can only be tested on the owner's phone. Stage 3 checks this first.
- While the Google app stays in Testing, sign-in expires every 7 days.

**Open questions for the owner:**
1. Is depending on Google Play services acceptable, and does your phone have it? If not, B builds the custom-scheme fallback instead, with a refresh token on the phone.
2. First run: a choice screen (my recommendation), or open the demo by default?
3. Should Disconnect only clear the account on the phone (my recommendation), or also remove the app's access at Google?
4. Is turning Android backup off for the whole app acceptable? Drafts would no longer be backed up. The alternative is to exclude only the stored account record and the Gmail profile.
5. Links on Android: keep them closed until track C decides (my recommendation), or should B add them now with a confirmation step?
6. Which Google account for the emulator (a throwaway one is best)? Will you sign it in yourself through the Device panel?
7. Same Google Cloud project as the desktop client, or a new one?

**Note for the coordinator:** the stages edit Android files that track A also touches: `AndroidManifest.xml`, `build.gradle.kts` and `MainActivity.kt`. The order of those edits needs agreeing with A.

Sources: [Google Developers Blog: custom URI scheme restrictions](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/improving-user-safety-in-oauth-flows-through-new-oauth-custom-uri-scheme-restrictions/), [Android Developers: Authorize access to Google user data](https://developer.android.com/identity/authorization), [Google Cloud help: Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)","textTruncated":false,"nextTextOffset":null,"updatedAt":"2026-11-21T13:37:25.715Z"}],"nextPosition":70,"hasMore":false,"earlierPosition":70}

## Decision (proposed)

### 1. Sign-in: option C, the Authorization API

- **OAuth client:** one **Android** client in the owner's Google Cloud project for each (package name, SHA-1) pair the app is signed with. The package name and the release/debug signing keys come from track A (ADR 0004). No Web client and no client secret. The custom URI scheme toggle stays **off**.
- **No client id in the build.** Play services matches package + signature. "Configured" therefore cannot be known before the first call. A `DEVELOPER_ERROR` result (package/SHA-1 not registered) maps to `not_configured`, with a next step that says this build is not registered. "Play services missing or too old" maps to `unsupported_platform` on connect. The account status says so plainly; it is not shown as an expired sign-in.
- **Bridge:** a Kotlin class in the Android app (`GoogleAuthBridge`), registered as an Android plugin from Rust with `tauri::plugin::Builder` and `register_android_plugin`. Rust calls it with `PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin` from worker threads, never from the main thread. **The webview cannot call it:** no plugin permission is added to `main-window`, and tokens never cross IPC. Operations:
  - `authorize(scopes, account?, interactive)` returns `{accessToken, grantedScopes, email}`, or one of `cancelled`, `needsUserInteraction`, `developerError`, `playServicesUnavailable`, `network` or `failed`.
  - `clearToken(token)`.
  - `revokeAccess(account, scopes)`.
  - `keystoreLoad`, `keystoreStore`, `keystoreClear` (section 2).
- **When UI is needed:** with `interactive = true`, the bridge launches the `PendingIntent` from `MainActivity` and resolves when the activity result arrives. Back or dismissing the sheet resolves `cancelled`, which maps to `AuthCancelled`. The existing 180 s `AUTH_TIMEOUT` and `CancelToken` still bound the wait on the Rust side. Silent calls (`interactive = false`) never show UI. If UI would be needed, they return `needsUserInteraction`, which maps to `AuthRequired` (**Sign-in expired** → **Sign in again**).
- **Account pinning:** when an account is already bound, the request pins it with `setAccount` so Play services does not offer a different account. The existing check still runs: `fetch_profile` must return the bound account, otherwise `AuthFailed` (`provider/api.rs:99-104`, `:250-262`).
- **What Rust reuses:** everything above the access token. That is `LiveGmailProvider`'s HTTP client, pacing, status and quota handling, account binding and credential-publication fences, `fetch_profile`, the scope verification, the sync worker, the operation ledger and the drafts. What is **not** used on Android is `authorize`, `wait_for_code`, `exchange_code` and `refresh` (`auth.rs:192-430`). They move behind a `CredentialSource` seam in `mail-core`:
  - `LoopbackPkceSource` is today's code, unchanged in behaviour, used on desktop.
  - `PlatformAuthorizerSource` sits over a small `PlatformAuthorizer` trait (`authorize`, `clear_token`, `revoke`). On Android its implementation is the bridge. In tests it is a scripted fake, so the whole Android path is tested on Linux.
- **Token lifetime on Android:** the access token lives only in process memory with its expiry. Before expiry, and after a 401, the source clears the cached token (`clearToken`) and calls `authorize(interactive = false)` **once**. A second failure is `AuthRequired`. No refresh token exists on the phone.

### 2. Token storage on Android

- `AndroidKeystoreSecrets` implements `Secrets`. It stores the serialized `TokenBundle` encrypted with an AES-256-GCM Keystore key (alias `email-os-gmail-binding`, no user authentication required, so sync can run while the app is open and unlocked). The file is in `noBackupFilesDir`. Under option C the bundle holds **no token material**: only the account id, the address and the granted scopes (section 4). The token fields stay in the type for desktop. On Android they are always empty, and a test asserts the stored JSON has no token.
- **No plaintext fallback.** A missing key, a failed decryption, a corrupt file or a Keystore error all return `SecretsUnavailable`, shown as today. **Disconnect** (`clear`) deletes the file and the key; it is the documented way to recover from a broken store. The fixture never touches it.
- **Backup and reinstall.** The manifest sets `android:allowBackup="false"`, plus `android:dataExtractionRules` and `android:fullBackupContent` that exclude everything. Keystore keys are never backed up, so a restored ciphertext could not be decrypted anyway. This also means local drafts and the demo mailbox are not backed up or moved to a new phone. That is consistent with "drafts are local to this device", but it is a visible change (owner question 4). An uninstall deletes app data and the Keystore key. A reinstall starts at the first-run screen and needs **Connect Gmail** again. Google still remembers the grant, so the consent screen may be skipped; the account chooser can still appear.
- `KeychainSecrets` keeps failing closed on Linux and Windows. Desktop is unchanged.

### 3. Mode selection, first run and what the fixture becomes

- **Mode file (Android only).** `<app_data_dir>/mode.json` holds `{"mode":"fixture"|"gmail"}`. It is written atomically (temp file + rename + fsync). Desktop keeps `EMAIL_OS_MODE` and ignores the file. On Android, `EMAIL_OS_MODE` stays ignored.
- **Session swap.** `AppState` holds the per-profile parts (core, draft service, subscription) as one `Session` behind a lock, replaced as a unit. Two new commands are added to `main-window`, the generated types and the manifest tests:
  - `get_mode_choice` returns `{chosen: bool, mode}`.
  - `switch_mode(mode)` stops the current core (releasing its `profile.lock`), opens the other profile, writes `mode.json`, swaps the session and emits `mode_changed`.
  
  The frontend reloads the window when `mode_changed` arrives. A command already running against the old core finishes against a stopped core and gets a typed error. Its result is discarded by the reload. The two profiles stay in separate directories (`fixture-profile`, `gmail-profile`) as on desktop, so a swap never mixes data.
- **First run.** If `mode.json` is absent, setup opens the fixture core as today, and `StartupRoot` shows a **choice screen** before any mailbox. The screen offers connecting your own mail account or opening the demo mailbox, and says that the demo is synthetic and nothing in it is sent anywhere. It follows the existing `FixtureTransitionGate` pattern. The legacy fixture transition gate, if pending, comes first. Choosing the demo writes `mode.json`. Choosing your own mail switches to Gmail mode, which shows **Not connected** with **Connect Gmail**, and starts Connect directly. A phone upgraded from an earlier fixture-only APK has no mode file, so it sees the choice once. Its demo data is kept.
- **Moving between modes.** The compact **Account** page shows in demo mode a **Use your own mail** row (→ `switch_mode("gmail")`), and in Gmail mode a **Switch to demo mailbox** row (→ `switch_mode("fixture")`). Switching to the demo **does not disconnect**: credentials, cache and drafts of the Gmail profile stay, and switching back resumes them. **Disconnect** keeps its desktop meaning: it is local, clears the binding and the Gmail cache, and keeps drafts. On Android it also calls `clearToken`. It does **not** revoke the Google grant unless the owner chooses that (owner question 3). After disconnect the app stays in Gmail mode on **Not connected**, where **Switch to demo mailbox** is available.
- **Phone layout.** The existing compact Account page and status lines (UX-14, development guide "Account, connection and first run") carry the Gmail states. The only copy change is the sign-in wait line: "Finish sign-in in your browser" becomes a phone-appropriate sentence, because the sheet is a system screen on the phone, not a browser. No new third-party brand names are added to UI copy; existing action names (**Connect Gmail**, **Sign in again**, **Enable mailbox actions**) stay as they are on desktop.
- **The fixture becomes the "demo mailbox".** It is the same ADR 0002 synthetic core, unchanged: first-run option, switch-back target, and the validation surface that needs no Google account. In a Gmail-capable build its account line is labelled as the demo so it is never mistaken for real mail. Desktop's default stays fixture.
- `androidFixture` in `App.vue` is renamed to what it means (`androidShell`). The gates in section 6 remain keyed to the platform, not to the mode.

### 4. Scopes and the upgrade mechanism

- **Granted scopes are a set.** `TokenBundle` gains `granted_scopes: Vec<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`). A legacy bundle with `gmail_modify_granted = true` is read as `{readonly, modify}`. The boolean is still written for one release so an older desktop build can read the bundle (desktop Keychain only).
- **Requests go through one function.** `GmailGrant` is a small enum. B ships `Readonly` and `Modify`. A grant maps to one scope string and one admission check. `GmailProvider::request_grant(grant, cancel)` replaces the body of `enable_mutations`. `enable_mutations` stays as the IPC-facing call and now calls `request_grant(Modify)`. A request always asks for the union of the scopes already granted and the new one:
  - desktop adds `include_granted_scopes=true` to the loopback request;
  - Android passes the full list to `authorize`.
  
  A grant counts only if the returned scope list contains it, for the same bound account. Asking is never evidence (`provider/api.rs:241-248` keeps that rule).
- **Read-only first, modify as an explicit upgrade:** unchanged on both platforms.
- **For track D:** D adds `GmailGrant::Send`, which maps to `gmail.send`. D owns the IPC command, the consent copy, the UI entry point and the send admission check that call `request_grant(Send)`. B adds no send scope, no send UI and no call site. Note for D's decision: Google documents `gmail.modify` as broader than this app's actions, and it already authorizes sending. Whether D still asks for a separate `gmail.send` grant is D's decision; the mechanism supports either.

### 5. Network and background behaviour

- **App open and in the foreground:** today's worker. The first sync runs after connect. Periodic sync runs every 60 s, with backoff up to 600 s. Manual **Sync now** works. Queued writes run as they do on desktop.
- **App in the background:** on window `Suspended` (Tauri 2.11, from `onPause`), the shell tells the core to **pause periodic sync**. A new `GmailCore::set_foreground(bool)` stops scheduling new periodic passes. It does not cancel a pass or a write already in flight. On `Resumed` (from `onResume`) the core resumes and runs one pass at once. A write in flight when Android freezes or kills the process is handled as on desktop after a crash. At the next start, globally applying operations become uncertain and are reconciled, never replayed blind.
- **App killed or swiped away:** nothing runs. The next launch restores the session silently. The binding is in Keystore, and the access token comes from a silent `authorize`. Then the first pass syncs.
- **Connectivity:** failures surface as today (**Sync failed · no network** with **Retry**). The bridge also registers a `ConnectivityManager` default-network callback while the app is in the foreground. When a network becomes available it calls `request_sync()` once, so recovery does not wait for the backoff.
- **Battery and data:** no foreground service, no WorkManager, no alarms, no wake locks. The 100-conversation cache cap and the existing pacing bound how much is fetched. There is no special handling for metered networks.
- **Out of scope:** push notifications (Gmail push needs Cloud Pub/Sub and a server, plus FCM), sync or sends while backgrounded or killed, scheduled background work, and notification badges.

### 6. Android-only gates

- **Stay closed:** attachment **export** (`save_attachment` → `UnsupportedPlatform`). Android has no "inert file in Downloads" equivalent without a MediaStore or Storage Access Framework design, and that needs its own decision. Gmail attachment *descriptors* still load through the core, but **Files and links** stays hidden on Android as today.
- **Stay closed in this track:** `open_external_link`. Opening a link from mail on the phone is part of reading mail, and track C (HTML mail, ADR 0006) owns how links in bodies behave. The bridge added here would make an `ACTION_VIEW` dispatch, behind the existing `validated_external_url` check and explicit confirmation, a small change. It is listed under Dependencies, not built here (owner question 5).
- **Open with Gmail on Android:** connect, sign in again, cancel sign-in, enable mailbox actions, sync now, disconnect, provider destinations, provider search and the provider-backed mailbox actions. These are the same commands desktop Gmail mode admits. The core decides by session policy, not by platform.

## Scope

input.message:
Coordinator review of ADR 0005 @ 8006b69. Very good: the Authorization API with no refresh token on the phone, the `CredentialSource`/`PlatformAuthorizer` seam with a scripted fake, the Keystore-encrypted binding with no token material, and the scope set with one `request_grant` are all approved in direction. Revise these points, push, and report `ADR READY` again. Do not implement yet.

1. Emulator facts (I checked): `emulator-5554` is a Google Play image (`sdk_gphone64_x86_64`) with `com.android.vending` and `com.google.android.gms` versionName 24.23.35. Update the risk: check whether that version supports the Authorization API you need, and say so; the emulator can probably run the real flow with a throwaway Google account.
2. The 7-day expiry in Testing mode will make the app unusable week to week. Add the alternative to the owner actions and recommend one: publishing status "In production" without verification for personal use (the owner is the only user, under the 100-user cap; Google shows an "unverified app" screen at consent), vs staying in Testing with weekly re-consent. Be precise about what Google documents for restricted Gmail scopes in each case and cite it; if unclear, say what to check.
3. Ordering with track A: A's ADR 0004 renames the package to `dev.exedev.emailos` (pending owner approval) and moves `src-tauri/gen/android/.../androidfixture/` → the new path, and also sets `allowBackup=false` with exclusion rules. A lands first; B builds on A's merged manifest and Kotlin paths and does not duplicate the backup change. Put this in Dependencies and drop your own backup-off item (point to A's). Your owner question 4 then goes away.
4. Track C will own links in mail bodies on Android. Keep `open_external_link` closed in B as you propose; I'll tell C it may use your bridge pattern or its own.
5. For track D: since `gmail.modify` already allows sending, D will be told to request `gmail.send` only when the account does not have modify. Make sure `request_grant` can report "already covered" without a consent screen.
6. Session swap: `switch_mode` stops the core and reloads the window. Say what happens to a draft open in the editor at the time (it must be saved first or the switch refused while an editor has unsaved changes).

I'll put your owner questions 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 to the owner together with the other tracks' questions and pass the answers back.

The ADR is on `usable/html-reader` as Proposed, under number 0006 as corrected. I have not written any code or run any builds.

**What I found in the code**
- **HTML-only messages disappear today.** The Gmail parser keeps only the `text/plain` part. A message with no text part is left out of the conversation entirely, and only a count of missing messages is shown.
- **The cache only stores text.** There is no column for HTML, and attachment records do not include a `Content-ID`, so `cid:` images cannot be matched to their attachments.
- **The 16 MiB limit per sync page fails the whole page if exceeded.** Adding HTML without changing that would break sync on large newsletters.

**What I propose**
- **Data:** keep both the text and the HTML part. For HTML-only mail, make a text version in Rust with the `html2text` crate; previews, search, the reply quote and "Copy message text" keep using text. HTML is capped at 512K characters per message and 2 MiB per conversation, stored in a new column added by migration 10, and loaded only when a message is expanded through a new read-only command. If a sync page would go over 16 MiB, the HTML is dropped and the text kept, instead of failing the page.
- **Sanitising:** DOMPurify in the frontend, at a pinned version. One code path then covers macOS, Android and the browser preview, and it uses the same parser that displays the result. CSS gets its own filter.
- **Isolation:** each message goes in an iframe with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and no `allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups` or `allow-top-navigation`. The frame also gets its own CSP, so no mail script can run and none can reach Tauri IPC.
- **Remote content:** remote images, including tracking pixels, are blocked by default. A per-message "Load images" lasts until the conversation is closed. For it to work in Tauri, the app's CSP must also allow `https:` images. `cid:` images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are fetched through the existing attachment path and load without asking, since they come from the message itself.
- **Links:** links in the mail can't navigate; every click opens one confirmation shared with Files and links. On Android it offers "Copy link" only until track B turns link opening on there.
- **Layout:** images are first limited to the column width; if the message is still too wide, it is scaled down to fit (not below half size) and scrolls sideways after that. The app is dark only, so mail with its own colours shows on a white card and mail without colours takes the app's colours; nothing is inverted. Trailing quotes collapse behind the existing "Show quoted text". Keyboard shortcuts keep working after clicking into a message.
- **Fixtures:** six new synthetic conversations, `conv-19` to `conv-24`: a newsletter with a tracking pixel, an HTML-only message, a `cid:` image, an HTML reply chain, a hostile sample (scripts, `javascript:` links, forms, `<base>`, CSS `@import`/`url()`, mXSS shapes) and an oversized one. Remote URLs use `.invalid`, and the Rust provider and browser preview share the same sample files.
- **Plan:** eight stages, starting with a test in real Chrome that checks the sandbox, CSP and scaling before any product code.

**Things that need you or another track**
- **macOS:** this machine can't run the macOS webview, so after stage 7 someone needs to run a 15-minute checklist on the Mac, plus an optional look at real newsletters.
- **Track B (0005):** they need to decide whether links open on Android in this programme. Track C reads a single frontend flag, `externalLinksAvailable`, so B can turn it on without changes to the reader.
- **Track D (0007):** sending can use the new read-only command if it wants HTML for forwards.

**Open questions**
1. **Same-origin frame:** your brief says no same-origin, and the ADR departs from that. Without it, the app can't size each frame to its message, catch link clicks or collapse quotes in a conversation holding several messages. Scripts stay off either way. Do you accept same-origin with no scripts, or do you want fully isolated frames of fixed height with links reachable only through Files and links?
2. **"Load images":** per message for one visit only, as proposed, or also remembered per sender?
3. **Inbox size:** going from 18 to 24 synthetic conversations changes tests and docs that say 18. Is that acceptable, or should the HTML samples replace the bodies of existing conversations?
4. **New dependencies:** are `dompurify` (npm) and `html2text` (Rust, which brings in `html5ever`) acceptable?
5. **`mailto:` links:** "Copy address" only, or also a "New message to …" that opens the existing compose?

content.text: ADR 0006 (HTML display) is in. Its technical questions I can settle myself; sending the review.

input.message:
Coordinator review of ADR 0006 @ 4de4826. Good work; finding that HTML-only messages vanish today, and the 16 MiB page failure, matter. Decisions on your questions and changes to make; then push and report `ADR READY` again. Do not implement yet.

Decisions (mine, technical):
1. Same-origin frame: accepted, `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` with no `allow-scripts`, on condition that stage 1's test proves no script runs in the frame by any route, including scripts the native webview injects into frames (Tauri's IPC/init scripts on WKWebView and Android WebView): assert from the parent that the frame's window has no `__TAURI_INTERNALS__`/`__TAURI__`/`ipc` and that an inline handler and a `javascript:` URL inside it never fire. Repeat that check on the Android emulator in validation, since Chromium-in-test is not the Android WebView path. Write down the srcdoc CSP inheritance (srcdoc frames inherit the embedder's CSP) and the exact app-CSP change for `https:` images, scoped as narrowly as possible.
2. Dependencies: `dompurify` (pinned, with the version in the ADR) and `html2text` are approved.
3. Fixtures: add `conv-19`–`conv-24` as proposed; update tests/docs that say 18/16 in a dedicated, mechanical stage. Don't overwrite existing conversation bodies.
4. `mailto:`: offer both "Copy address" and "New message to …" opening the existing compose with To filled.
5. Links on Android: track C owns opening links from mail bodies on Android in this programme (it's part of reading mail), not track B. Add a stage: confirmation as on desktop, then `ACTION_VIEW` dispatch through `validated_external_url` (tauri-plugin-opener or a small Kotlin intent; pick and justify; no new IPC that lets mail content open URLs without the confirmation). Keep "Copy link" in the confirmation. Your `externalLinksAvailable` flag then turns on for Android. Attachment saving on Android stays out of scope.

Changes:
6. Verify "the app is dark only" against the code (`src/assets/*`, theme tokens) and cite it; if a light theme exists, cover both.
7. Remote images: "Load images" per message for one visit stays the default. Whether it is also remembered per sender is an owner question; write it as an option with your recommendation.
8. In the implementation plan, mark which stages touch the shared reader components that tracks D (send: reply/compose, thread refresh after send) and A (startup) also touch, so I can order merges.

The macOS checklist as an owner action is fine; keep it to 15 minutes.

content.text: Before I approve the ADRs I need your call on some product and setup decisions. Two short rounds of questions.

questions.question: Android app ID: changing it means one fresh install (the demo app can stay alongside). It must be fixed before the Google sign-in is registered, because Google ties sign-in to it. Which ID?

options.label: dev.exedev.emailos (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the desktop ID prefix (dev.exedev.email-os.fixture). The launcher label becomes "Email OS".

options.label: Keep androidfixture
options.description: No ID change now, but the name says 'fixture' forever, or a second reinstall later.

questions.question: Does the phone you'll use have Google Play services (the Play Store)? Please put the model and Android version in the notes.

options.label: Yes, it has the Play Store (Recommended)
options.description: Sign-in uses Google's own Android sign-in screen; no long-lived Google token is stored on the phone.

options.label: No Play services
options.description: Sign-in uses a browser tab that returns to the app, and a Google refresh token is stored on the phone (encrypted).

questions.question: Sending can't be undone (no 'Undo send' window, in line with your earlier 'endings stay quiet' rule). Should every Send show a confirmation?

options.label: No dialog, Send acts at once (Recommended)
options.description: Recipients and subject always visible in the editor; Send sits apart from X. Status (queued, sending, failed, unknown) shows quietly in Drafts/Activity.

options.label: Confirmation sheet every time
options.description: A sheet shows From, To/Cc and subject; tap Send again to confirm. Safer, one extra tap per message.

questions.question: First launch of the Android app: what should it show?

options.label: Choice: your mail or the demo (Recommended)
options.description: One screen offering 'Connect Gmail' or 'Open the demo mailbox'. Switchable later from the Account page.

options.label: Go straight to Gmail sign-in
options.description: The demo mailbox stays reachable only from the Account page.

Owner decision for ADR 0007 (fold into your revision; record it in a "Decisions" section dated 2026-11-21): **Undo send, available for only a few seconds. No confirmation dialog.** Design it as:
- Send acts at once from the editor (recipients and subject always visible; Send placed apart from X). The editor closes and an "Undo" action is shown for a short window: use 5 seconds unless you find a strong reason otherwise, and state it.
- During the window the intent is queued with a not-before time and is not dispatched. Undo atomically cancels before the dispatch barrier and reopens the draft in the editor unchanged. If the app is killed during the window, on restart the intent is still pre-dispatch: say whether it then sends or returns to the draft (recommend returning it to Drafts as "not sent" rather than sending without the user having seen the window end).
- After the window, the existing states apply (sending, sent, failed, unknown); keep those quiet in Drafts/Activity, no extra toasts.
- Offline during the window: the window still ends; the intent stays queued until online.
This replaces my point 4 (confirmation dialog question). Update the UI, ledger states, synthetic provider tests, and validation (a recording showing Undo within the window and a send after it).

19-## Context
20-
21-The Android build is a fixture-only app. One person should be able to use it with their own Gmail account. This ADR decides how the phone signs in, where it keeps credentials, how the user moves between the demo mailbox and Gmail, and what runs when.
22-
23-What exists today:
24-
25-- **Mode is fixed on Android.** `src-tauri/src/setup.rs:41-42` sets `#[cfg(mobile)] let mode = "fixture"`. Desktop reads `EMAIL_OS_MODE` (`setup.rs:43-49`) and opens `gmail-profile` with `LiveGmailProvider::from_env(Arc::new(KeychainSecrets::new()))` (`setup.rs:53-58`). The choice is made once, at setup. `AppState` holds one `GmailCore` and one `DraftService` for the life of the process (`src-tauri/src/state.rs:8-14`). Nothing can swap them at runtime.
26-- **OAuth is the desktop loopback flow.** `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs:192` `authorize` makes a PKCE verifier, challenge and state (`auth.rs:177`). It binds `127.0.0.1:0` and opens the URL with the `webbrowser` crate (`auth.rs:144`). It then waits up to `AUTH_TIMEOUT` = 180 s for the exact callback path and state (`auth.rs:239`). `exchange_code` (`auth.rs:382`) and `refresh` (`auth.rs:404`) talk to the token endpoint. The client id comes from `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` in the launch environment (`GoogleConfig::from_env`, `auth.rs:70`). If it is missing, the app reports a visible `not_configured`. A phone has no launch environment.
27-- **Scopes.** The first connection asks only for `gmail.readonly` (`auth.rs:27`, `provider/api.rs:206-226`). **Enable mailbox actions** asks for `gmail.modify` (`provider/api.rs:72-95`). The grant is stored as a single boolean, `TokenBundle.gmail_modify_granted` (`secrets.rs:30`). It becomes true only when the token response lists the modify scope (`provider.rs:585`). It is bound to the account that first connected (`provider/api.rs:99-104`). The upgrade request does not set `include_granted_scopes`, so a third scope has nowhere to go.
28-- **Token custody.** The `Secrets` trait (`secrets.rs:54-61`) has one production implementation, `KeychainSecrets`, which uses the macOS Keychain. On every other platform, Android included, it returns `SecretsUnavailable` (`secrets.rs:119-132`). There is no plaintext fallback, by design. `LiveGmailProvider::access_token` (`provider.rs:221`) loads the bundle and refreshes it with the stored refresh token (`provider.rs:262`). Credential publication is fenced so a disconnect or account change during OAuth cannot be overwritten (`provider.rs:76-92`, `provider/api.rs:110-130`).
29-- **Disconnect** clears the secret (`provider/api.rs:314-324`) and the core clears the Gmail cache. Drafts stay on the device. Google's grant is not revoked (`docs/development.md`, "Google Desktop OAuth setup").
--
203-| **External, Testing** | "Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent". The only exception is apps that request nothing beyond name, email and profile, so Gmail scopes get the 7-day rule. At most 100 test users ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945); [OAuth 2.0: refresh token expiration](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration)). | **Sign-in expired** every week; **Sign in again** shows the consent screen again. Usable for a validation run, not for daily use. |
204-| **External, In production, not verified** | The app "might display an 'unverified app' screen before it displays the consent screen" ([Unverified apps](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). It is limited to "100 new users in total", over the project's lifetime ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)). The restricted-scope verification page names personal use as a case where verification may not be needed: "if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you" ([Restricted scope verification](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification)). Google states the 7-day expiry **only** for Testing. It does **not** say whether authorizations last longer for an unverified production app with restricted scopes. The general expiry rules (six months unused; password change for Gmail scopes) still apply. | The owner clicks through the unverified-app screen at each consent. That expected screen is the only ongoing cost. **Unconfirmed:** whether consent survives past 7 days. To check, at least 8 days after consent, kill and relaunch the app; it must sync with no sign-in UI (validation plan). |
205:| **Personal mode** (user type chosen when the project is created) | "Personal mode apps do not require OAuth app verification, are not subject to the OAuth user cap or 7-day test user token expiration, and do not display the unverified app screen." "Only the Google Account that created the Personal mode application can sign in or authorize scopes for its OAuth clients." It is "a one-time selection when configuring a new application": an existing project cannot switch. Android is listed as a client type ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945); [Personal mode onboarding](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15544987#personal-mode-onboarding)). These pages do not list scope restrictions, and they do not say explicitly that restricted Gmail scopes are allowed. Workspace accounts "might still require configuration by your organization's administrators". | Fits a one-person app exactly: no weekly expiry, no unverified screen, no cap. It needs a **new** project, created **by the account whose mail the phone reads**. **To check at setup:** **Data access** accepts the Gmail scopes, and the first Connect shows no unverified-app screen. |
206-
207:**Recommendation:** **Personal mode**, in a new project created by the Google account the owner will read on the phone. If it does not accept the Gmail scopes, or is not offered for that account, use **External, In production, not verified**. Keep the "unverified app" screen at consent, and confirm the 8-day check before relying on it. **Testing** is only for a throwaway validation account. Because a Personal project accepts only its creator, a throwaway emulator account needs its own small project: either its own Personal project created while signed in as that account, or an External Testing project where it is a test user.
208-
209-### Steps
210-
211:1. **Create the project.** For Personal mode, open the Personal mode onboarding (Google Cloud console → Google Auth Platform → Overview → personal onboarding, `console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview/personal`) while signed in as the account the phone will read. Otherwise use an External project. Enable **Gmail API** under **APIs & Services → Library**.
212-2. **Google Auth Platform → Branding:** app name, user support email, developer contact. No logo is needed.
213-3. **Google Auth Platform → Audience** (External projects only):
214-   - For daily use, set **Publish app** to **In production**, with no verification submission.
215-   - For a throwaway validation project, keep **Testing** and add the throwaway account as a **Test user**.
216-4. **Google Auth Platform → Data access:** add `.../auth/gmail.readonly` and `.../auth/gmail.modify`. Track D adds `.../auth/gmail.send` only for accounts without modify. Do not submit for verification.
217-5. **Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create client → Android:**
218-   - Package name: `dev.exedev.emailos` (Decision 4) for both clients.
219-   - **Release client:** the SHA-1 of the owner's release certificate. ADR 0004's owner steps print it (`keytool -list -v -keystore <release.jks> -alias <alias>`). Register it in the project the owner uses daily.
220-   - **Debug client:** `93:06:D5:83:0B:27:BE:95:BB:48:80:7B:52:9C:95:D5:C8:18:C6:03`, this VM's debug key. Register it in the project whose account signs in on the emulator.
221-   
222-   Leave **Advanced settings → custom URI scheme** off. No Web client, no secret. No client id has to be sent to me or put in the build. If Google refuses a pair as "already in use", it is registered in another client; delete it there first.
223-6. **For the emulator run:** sign a throwaway Google account into the emulator yourself through the T3 Device panel (**Settings → Passwords & accounts**, or the account chooser during Connect). I never type, see or store the password. Put a few synthetic messages in that account so the recording contains no real mail. With an account signed in, the emulator's Play Store can update Google Play services if stage 3 finds the installed version too old.
--
309-- A screen recording (≤60 s) of Connect through first sync. It contains the account address and mail, so it is **not committed**. It is kept in `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/android-gmail/` and listed in the PR, unless the account holds only synthetic mail and the owner agrees to commit it.
310-- On the owner's phone (after track A): install, Connect, sync, Enable mailbox actions, archive + Undo, background/resume. The owner reports the results; no screenshots of real mail are committed.
311:- **Lasting sign-in:** at least 8 days after the owner's first consent on the phone, in the project set up for daily use (Personal mode, or In production unverified), kill and relaunch the app. It must sync with no sign-in UI. This is the check for what Google does not document (Owner actions). The owner reports the result.
312-
313-## Risks and open questions
314-
315-**Risks**
316-
317-- **Play services dependency.** Phones without Google Play services cannot connect; they keep the demo mailbox. The owner accepted this (Decision 1).
318-- **Debug keystore drift.** If this VM's `~/.android/debug.keystore` is regenerated, emulator sign-in fails with `not_configured` until the new SHA-1 is registered.
319-- **Emulator Play services version.** The emulator runs Play services 24.23.35 (about June 2024) and has the Play Store.
320-  - What Google documents: `authorize()` fails "if authorization is not available on the device (for example, internal error or Play Services not available)", and unsupported calls "fail with an ApiException" ([AuthorizationClient reference](https://developers.google.com/android/reference/com/google/android/gms/auth/api/identity/AuthorizationClient); [Play services release notes](https://developers.google.com/android/guides/releases)). `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` were added in play-services-auth **21.4.0 (July 2025)**. I found no documented minimum Play services APK version for any of these calls.
321-  - Inferred, not documented: `authorize()` predates the 21.x library releases, so 24.23.35 very likely supports it. Then the emulator can run the real flow with a throwaway Google account. `clearToken` may be missing from a June 2024 Play services (B does not use `revokeAccess`).
322-  - Handling: stage 3's probe records what the emulator supports. The bridge treats a missing `clearToken` as `unsupported` and degrades as described in section 1. With a throwaway account signed in, the Play Store can update Play services; an update changes the emulator, so it needs the coordinator's agreement. The owner's phone, with current Play services, is the final check either way.
323-- **Bridge mechanics.** A blocking `run_mobile_plugin` call that waits on an activity result must not deadlock with the main thread, and the `PendingIntent` result must reach the bridge after a configuration change. Stage 3 proves this before anything depends on it.
324:- **Consent lifetime.** Testing expires every 7 days (documented). Personal mode documents no 7-day expiry, but its pages do not say explicitly that restricted Gmail scopes are allowed. Unverified production has no documented 7-day rule but no positive statement either. The 8-day check in the validation plan settles it for the chosen setup.
325-- **Process freeze in background.** Android may freeze or kill the process during a write. This relies on the existing outcome-unknown reconciliation; no new guarantee is claimed.
326-- **Package rename by track A** after the Android client is registered means a new client. Register only after A's rename is merged.
327-
328-**Open questions for the owner**
329-
330-Questions 1–3 were decided on 2026-11-21 (see Decisions), and 4–5 were resolved by the coordinator. Still open:
331-
332-6. Which **Google account** will be used on the emulator? A throwaway one is recommended, holding only synthetic mail. Will you sign it in yourself through the Device panel when stage 7 starts? This also decides which project holds the debug client.
333:7. **Same Cloud project as desktop, or a new one?** A Personal mode project must be new, because existing projects cannot switch to Personal. Desktop can keep its current project, or add a Desktop client in the new one later.
334:8. **Publishing setup for daily use:** Personal mode (recommended), In production without verification, or Testing with weekly re-consent? See Owner actions.

questions.question: Google sign-in setup for daily use on your phone. Google's 'Testing' mode makes sign-in expire every 7 days. Which publishing setup?

options.label: Personal mode (Recommended)
options.description: A new Google Cloud project created by the Google account you'll read on the phone. No weekly expiry, no 'unverified app' screen, only that account can sign in. Not yet confirmed that Google allows the Gmail scopes here; we check at setup.

options.label: In production, unverified
options.description: Works in an existing project; shows an 'unverified app' warning at each consent. Google doesn't say whether consent lasts past 7 days; an 8-day check settles it.

**What I'll start next:**
- Google sign-in starts when the install work merges, because it depends on the new app ID.
- Sending starts when the HTML work merges. Most of it can be built before Google sign-in lands; only the live-Gmail step waits for it.

**Design calls I made myself:**
- **HTML mail** shows in an isolated frame where no scripts can run. The thread has to prove that on the emulator too, not just in the browser.
- **Opening links on Android** is part of the HTML work, with the same confirmation step as desktop.

- I set the Undo send window to 5 seconds. If the app is killed during those 5 seconds, the message goes back to Drafts as "Not sent" rather than sending.

**What I need from you:**
1. **Your phone's model and Android version.**
2. **The signing key**, whenever you're ready. You create it on your own computer with the two commands in ADR 0004 ("Owner actions", step 1) and send me only the SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints. Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

**First request:** "What's left to do on the Android app before I can actually use it?" Answered. The phone UI is done (PR #80 merged 2026-11-19), but:
- Android is locked to the demo mailbox.
- There is no token storage outside the macOS Keychain, and OAuth is desktop loopback only.
- There is no sending, no HTML display, and no attachment saving or link opening on Android.
- Builds are debug-signed, the first launch can ANR, and it has never run on a physical phone.

**Current request** (arrived through a context handoff after its first turn failed to start; full text in section 6): run four scoping threads, each in its own worktree:

- Google SSO on Android: Opus 5.5 High, with a **new** ADR rather than an edit of the earlier one
- HTML display: Opus 5.5 High
- Sending on desktop and Android: GPT-6.2-SOL, no effort given; I used high

Workflow the user asked for:
1. Each thread proposes an ADR.
2. I review it and, once happy, give the greenlight to implement.
3. Each thread implements with GPT-6.1-Terra High subagents and reviews the implementation itself before asking me to review.
4. Review of the implementation should include validation with screenshots and videos where applicable.

**Owner answers (AskUserQuestion, 2026-11-21):**
- Pacing: ADRs together, **build 2 tracks at a time**. The option text gave the order as signing + HTML first, then Google sign-in, then sending.
- Merging: "PR to main, I merge". The option description was "I merge each PR to main myself once my review and CI pass", so Claude merges each PR after its review and CI.
- Desktop sending: macOS only.
- Clear `target/debug/incremental`: yes (done).
- App ID: `dev.exedev.emailos`.
- Phone: has Google Play services. Model and Android version were asked for in the notes but **not given**.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts
- Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + TypeScript; Rust core `crates/mail-core`; shell `src-tauri`. GitHub repo `BbrSofiane/email-os` is PUBLIC.
- **A, ADR 0004:**
  - release APK signed by an owner-held JKS key; CI workflow "Android Release" (manual dispatch on main, protected `android-release` environment)

  - `<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin" srcdoc>` without scripts, plus a frame CSP; remote images blocked by default
  - fixtures `conv-19`..`conv-24`; `tauri-plugin-opener` 2.5.5 called from Rust only for Android links
- **D, ADR 0007:**
  - `users.messages.send`; immutable ledger intent; `local-drafts` kept separate with the ledger authoritative
  - 5 s Undo window before dispatch; a restart inside the window returns the draft as "Not sent"
  - unknown outcomes are never replayed; "Copy to a new draft" and Dismiss on unknown rows
  - changed-subject replies omit `threadId`

Review of PR #92 @ bc5d5bf: CHANGES REQUESTED, not merged. CI is green, and the sanitiser, frame, IPC and Android link code read well. I read those, the parse/store parts of mail-core, and looked at the Android screenshots, a sample of the browser ones, and the recording. I have not re-run your gates. Must fix: 1. **A sender can exhaust memory during sync (`parse.rs` `html_to_text`).** It runs on any HTML-only body up to MAX_PART_BODY_BYTES (1 MiB), before the 512 Ki HTML cap, and `.take(MAX_MESSAGE_TEXT_CHARS)` applies only after html2text has built its whole output. With html2text 0.17.3, plain_no_decorate + link_footnotes, width 10_000, release build, desktop x86_64: - one table row with 50,000 `a` (500 KB in) → a 500,200,001-byte string, 1.9 s; - 90,000 nested `
` (990 KB) → 18.6 s; 10,000 → 0.25 s (so roughly quadratic); - 10,000 nested `
` or `
  • ` → `TooNarrow`, so the message counts as having no displayable body. These `?`-style failures lose the body even though its HTML would be shown. On a phone this could kill sync on every attempt. I did not run it inside the app. Bound the work before converting (input size, nesting depth, table cells) and bound output while building it, or replace the conversion for over-limit input with a simple bounded text extraction. Over-limit input must still yield some text or a clear state, and must never make the page or sync fail. Add tests for these shapes with a size and time bound, including several such messages in one thread. 2. **CSS filter disagrees with the browser on newlines in strings (`css-filter.ts`).** The browser ends a string at a raw newline; the filter stays inside it. `a { x: "\n; background: url(https://tracker/p.png); y: "; }` (real newline) passes with `remoteImages: false` and `blockedRemote: 0`. I confirmed in Chrome 156 that the browser then requests the URL when there is no CSP, and that your frame CSP blocks it. So there is no leak today, but one of the two layers is bypassed, `position: fixed` gets through the same way, and the header comment claims malformed input cannot leak. Treat \n, \r and \f inside a string as malformed and drop; check other tokenizer differences (bad url tokens, unbalanced brackets in at-rule preludes, CDO/CDC, NUL). Add corpus cases for both `

Neither build track has merged yet. The HTML PR needs fixes, and the install track has been stuck on the emulator since yesterday afternoon.

**Your answers**
1. **Phone:** Nothing Phone (3a) Pro on Android 17 is passed on to the install track. The emulator runs Android 15, so Android 17 only gets tested on your phone.
2. **Signing key:** the file is on this VM, but you chose to keep the key on your computer and in GitHub only. It is also readable by every user on this machine, and the agents run as your user. I checked only its listing and first four bytes; I haven't opened, moved or changed it, and I told the install thread to leave it alone.
   - It looks like PKCS12, not the JKS format the ADR assumes. I've asked the install track to support both.
   - I can't get the fingerprints without its password.
3. **Throwaway account:** keep it ready. You'll need it when the sign-in track reaches its emulator step.

**Track status**

| Track | Status |
|---|---|
| [A: install](t3-thread://v2/a54b6c0e-579e-4ecd-b328-bf6fee0ad1e4/mcp:launch:573c8819cbb80a78893c9abd59cc00063bb4207ea13820a520e1ac231cd7228a) | Stage 1 done. Startup diagnosis is blocked; it's continuing with the parts that don't need the emulator |

| B: Google sign-in, D: sending | Approved, waiting for a slot |

**Why I sent the HTML PR back**
- **Hostile mail could stall or crash sync:** in my stress test, a 500 KB message expanded to 500 MB of text, and another took 18 seconds to convert. I tested the conversion library on its own, not inside the app.
- **The style filter can be bypassed:** a crafted message gets a tracking image past it. The frame's second layer blocked the request in Chrome, so I found no actual leak.
- **The recording is out of date:** it shows a newsletter opening as an empty strip, a bug fixed later that day. I asked for a new recording and screenshots from the final build.

**What I need from you**
1. **Can you free the emulator?** The earlier mobile-layout coordinator conversation still holds it (session `t3-589cdd0c7ee86c624c29dbea`, last updated 18 November). Close the device in that thread, or tell me if I may close that session.
2. **Where should the signing key live?** I recommend creating a new one on your computer with the ADR 0004 commands, then deleting the VM copy; as far as I know, nothing has been signed with it. Send me only the SHA-1 and SHA-256 from that `keytool -list -v` output. If you'd rather keep this key, move it off the VM and run this on your computer:
   ```sh
   keytool -list -v -keystore upload-keystore.jks
   ```

I don't get notified when these threads finish, so message me when you want the next check.
