Track C of the "usable Android app" programme. This PR implements [ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-html-mail-reader.md), now marked Accepted. Its "Implementation record" section lists five departures from the proposal and the validation results.

## What changes

- **Gmail parse (mail-core).** The parse keeps the HTML part next to the plain one. HTML-only mail is no longer dropped: its text comes from a bounded linear extractor (`html_text.rs`) and feeds previews, search, reply quotes and copying. The parse also reads the charset and records inline `cid:` parts. HTML is capped at 512 Ki characters per message and 2 MiB per thread. HTML and the text derived from it have their own 8 MiB page budget, so they never take room from ordinary threads; past it HTML is shown as "too large" and the derived text is cut to an excerpt.
- **Storage.** Migration `gmail-migrations-10` adds `body_html`, `html_state` and `inline_parts_json`. Cached mail stays plain until it is refreshed.
- **IPC.** There are two new read-only commands:
  - `get_message_html`;
  - `get_inline_image`: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP only, up to 2 MiB, signature-checked, returned as base64 with no disk writes.

  `Message.htmlBody` carries the state.
- **Sanitiser** (`src/lib/html-mail/`).
  - DOMPurify 3.4.17 (pinned) and a string-aware CSS filter clean the mail inside an inert document. The result is never parsed in the app document.
  - No `href` survives: link targets move to `data-eos-href`.
  - Remote images are held back as `data-eos-src` until Load images.
  - The reader marks and collapses the quote at the end of a reply.
- **Frame** (`HtmlMessageFrame.vue`).
  - A `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` only.
  - Its own CSP, `default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; …`, inside the app CSP. The app CSP's one change is `https:` in `img-src`.
  - A fail-closed guard falls back to text if any Tauri global is visible in the frame.
  - The frame fits its content's height and zooms wide mail down to a 0.5 floor, then scrolls sideways.
  - Mail with its own colours gets a paper card. Other mail uses the app's colours.
- **Reader.**
  - The "Remote images blocked. Load images" bar applies to one message until the conversation closes (owner decision).
  - Show plain text / Show formatted switch per message.
  - Notes for HTML that is too large or unavailable.
  - Shortcuts still work after clicking into a message.
- **Links.**
  - One confirmation shows the full URL and warns when the link text names a different host.
  - `mailto:` offers "Copy address" and "New message to …".
  - On Android, a confirmed link opens through `ACTION_VIEW` via JNI (`jni` 0.21.1, already in the lock graph), after `validated_external_url`. No new plugin or permission was added.
- **Fixtures.** Six synthetic HTML samples, `conv-19`..`conv-24`, raise the native fixture from 18 to 24 conversations. Synthetic seed v2 upgrades v1 profiles additively. The browser preview's primary workspace includes the samples; the fake's default test seed stays at 18.
- **Docs.** current-status, development, current-architecture, ux-02 and ux-12.

## Gates (head of this branch)

- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=… CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`: **passed** (exit 0). It covers:
  - mail-core tests, `check:contract`, fmt and clippy;
  - 133 frontend test files with 2163 tests, and typecheck;
  - `lint:native`, the bridge tests (18) and the web build.
- Rendered tests with Chrome 156 and `EMAIL_OS_RUN_RENDERED=1`: **34 passed, 1 skipped**. The suites are:
  - `tests/reader/html-reader.rendered.test.ts`;
  - `tests/reader/html-sanitize.rendered.test.ts`;
  - `tests/rendered/html-frame-spike.rendered.test.ts`;
  - `tests/reader/reader.rendered.test.ts`.
- `mise run android:build` (debug APK, aarch64 + x86_64): **passed**. That APK, built at `28e322a`, is installed on the emulator.
- Frame probe on the Android 15 WebView (Chrome 124), run over DevTools on an earlier APK built at `3196274` (not re-run on the `28e322a` APK; an earlier version of this text said otherwise): **37/37 PASS**. No script runs by any route, and no Tauri global is visible in any frame. The parent exposes `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` and `ipc`.

## Evidence

- `docs/validation/html-reader/browser/`: 20 PNGs, desktop (1100 px) and phone (390 px).
  - Newsletter blocked and loaded, HTML-only, cid image, reply collapsed and expanded, hostile sample, oversized.
  - Link confirmation and `mailto:` confirmation.
- `docs/validation/html-reader/android/`:
  - inbox, newsletter blocked, link confirmation, link opened in the system browser;
  - HTML-only, cid, reply chain, hostile, oversized;
  - a reopened conversation, the `mailto:` confirmation, New message with only To filled, long-press selection inside the frame;
  - font scale 1.35 (plan and newsletter).
- `docs/validation/html-reader/android/android-load-images-link.mp4` (31 s): open the newsletter → Load images → tap a link → confirmation → Open in browser → the system browser opens → Back returns to the reader.
- `docs/validation/html-reader/android-frame-probe.txt`: the probe output.

## Owner action: macOS check (about 15 minutes)

This VM cannot run WKWebView. On the Mac, run `pnpm tauri dev` on this branch with the native fixture profile:

1. Open `conv-19` (newsletter). It fits the column and the "Remote images blocked." bar shows. Load images shows alt text or broken images (the hosts are `.invalid`) and nothing else changes.
2. Open `conv-21`. The inline logo shows without Load images.
3. Open `conv-22`. The quoted part is collapsed, and Show quoted text opens it.
4. Open `conv-23` (hostile). The window title stays "email-os", no dialog appears and the text shows. The message is **not** replaced by "Formatted view unavailable".
5. Click a link in `conv-20`. The confirmation shows the full URL, Copy link works and Keep reading closes it. Click the `mailto:` link: New message opens with only To filled.
6. Click inside a message, then press `j`/`k`. Navigation still works.
7. Open the Web Inspector and select the app page. Paste `FRAME_PROBE_SOURCE` from `tests/rendered/html-frame-probe.ts` into the console and run it. Every line should be `PASS`. This repeats the no-script proof on WKWebView. The console should otherwise show only CSP reports for blocked images.

Twice the load average was 4–10, once about 2.7. "Wait" recovered each time. **Install's startup timings, from the Android 15 emulator:**
- The app opened to the inbox on all 11 launches.
- Two of the five first-ever launches showed "isn't responding" (10.8 s and 8.4 s). Each appeared before the app's own startup work began, while the system's web view was still being set up.
- None of the five launches with existing data showed it, and neither did the upgrade launch. A typical launch took about 6 s.
- On that evidence, the HTML reader isn't what causes the slow starts.

The emulator here is slow and the machine was under heavy load, so a real phone should be much faster. That's why your test decides it.

**What I need from you:** install the debug APK from the [newest build](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/actions/runs/45077584648) on your Nothing Phone. - roughly how long each launch takes to show the inbox.

**Disk is getting tight:** 2.2 GB free. The threads stop building below 2 GB, and sending's Android stage still needs a build. The shared build folder [`/home/exedev/email-os/target`](/home/exedev/email-os/target) holds 23 GB, which the next build would recreate. Should I clear it?

remove the stall. Test on a comparable emulator with a newer WebView and
on the physical phone before selecting a provider or lifecycle change.

Your phone result closes the last open condition on the install work, so I've moved [PR #93](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/93) out of draft. I'll merge it once CI passes on the new commit.

- **Your phone test:** I added your result to the install docs: about 2 seconds to the inbox and no "isn't responding". I've treated the freezes seen on the emulator as a problem with the emulator, not the app. If one ever shows up on your phone, the release block comes back. That doc update is the only new commit.
- **Recordings:** I checked install's three recordings. They show a fresh launch, the update keeping your Done item, and a draft surviving the update, all as described. The fresh-launch clip ends on the splash screen, but the separate inbox screenshot covers the rest.
- **Disk:** 21 GB free now, thanks. That's plenty for sending's Android build.

**Once it merges, I'll:**
- start the [Google sign-in](t3-thread://v2/a54b6c0e-579e-4ecd-b328-bf6fee0ad1e4/mcp:launch:ab75b75b3a99b75d5f2a1ff65f9c3e98aa00da2aaf123d5394148aa8b60d383b) track, which will run alongside sending;
- send you the steps for the `android-release` GitHub environment and its signing secrets, so you can make the first signed release.

Your phone test only covered startup. Testing an update in place on your phone needs that first signed release.

[Sending](t3-thread://v2/a54b6c0e-579e-4ecd-b328-bf6fee0ad1e4/mcp:launch:7bb2a69a2f020bea151d2d25d56e35433abdb57c17439337f593fb9ceb54771e) is still building the Send and Undo screens.
